Plus a direct unit test asserting `baton beads create --type warning --message "x"` parses and sets `args.content == "x"`.

title: Bead CLI swallows every backend exception and reports a false "No baton.db found" with exit 0
evidence: `_get_bead_store()` ends with `except BdNotAvailable: return None` / `except Exception: return None` (bead_cmd.py:111-114). Its own docstring (lines 94-102) states the opposite of what callers print: "ADR-13b WP-G: ``baton.db`` existence is NOT required... ``None`` is returned only on hard failures (``bd`` binary not on PATH, unexpected exception)". Yet every caller maps `None` to a baton.db message and returns 0 — e.g. line 668-670: `store = _get_bead_store()` / `if store is None: print("No baton.db found in .claude/team-context/ — no beads to list."); return`; same pattern at 702 (show), 716 (ready), 744 (close). Reproduced in a dir where `.claude/team-context/baton.db` DOES exist, with `BATON_BD_BIN=/nonexistent/bd`: `baton beads list` → "No baton.db found in .claude/team-context/ — no beads to list.", exit 0. Root CLAUDE.md documents `BATON_BD_BACKEND` as "`bd` is now the only supported value... raises `BdNotAvailable` if `bd` binary is missing" — the CLI defeats that.
why_it_matters: On any machine where `bd` is not on PATH (or `.beads/` is corrupt, or the workspace is unreadable), `baton beads list/show/ready/close` all report "nothing here" and exit 0. An operator sees an empty incident log and concludes the run was clean when in fact the bead subsystem is entirely dead. The message actively misdirects: it names a file that exists and is irrelevant, so the user searches for a missing DB instead of installing `bd`. docs/troubleshooting.md:368-383 even tells users to diagnose `bd`-not-found by running `baton beads list` — the one command guaranteed to hide it.
proposed_fix: Delete the blanket `except Exception: return None` at bead_cmd.py:113-114 and let unexpected errors reach `main.py`'s top-level handler. For `except BdNotAvailable as exc`, do not return `None` — call `user_error("bead backend unavailable: bd binary not found", hint="Install bd (see docs/troubleshooting.md) or set BATON_BD_BIN to its path.", exit_code=EXIT_RUNTIME)`. Reserve the `None`/exit-0 path for the genuinely empty case, and change the message to "No beads found (empty .beads/ workspace)."
test_strategy: With `BATON_BD_BIN` pointed at a nonexistent path, assert `baton beads list` exits non-zero and that stderr mentions `bd` (and does NOT contain the string "No baton.db found"). A second test must assert that with a working `bd` and an empty workspace, `baton beads list` still exits 0 and prints an empty-result message.

title: baton install never installs templates/skills/, producing a silently incomplete install
evidence: install.py:240 declares `skills_dir = base / "skills"` and includes it in the `mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)` loop at 243-250 — and that is the only occurrence of "skills" in the whole distribute package (`grep -rn skills agent_baton/cli/commands/distribute/*.py` returns exactly lines 240 and 248). No copy step exists. `scripts/install.sh:140-153` does copy them: `SKILLS_SRC="$ROOT_DIR/templates/skills"` … `for skill_dir in "$SKILLS_SRC"/*/; do … cp "$skill_dir"/* "$target_skill_dir/"`. `ls templates/skills` shows three real skills: `baton-beads`, `baton-help`, `baton-learn`. Reproduced: `baton install --scope project --source /home/user/agent-baton --verify` in a clean dir printed "Installed: 31 agents + 21 references + 3 agent templates" and `.claude/skills/` was empty. docs/cli-reference.md:44-51 presents the two installers as interchangeable ("# Deploy agent definitions… scripts/install.sh" / "# Or use the CLI installer / baton install --scope user --source …"), and README.md:162 says the installer installs "hooks, and skills".
why_it_matters: A user who follows the documented CLI path gets a project with an empty `.claude/skills/` directory — the `/baton-beads`, `/baton-help`, and `/baton-learn` skills silently do not exist. Nothing warns them; `--verify` (install.py:76-120) checks agents, references, templates/agents, team-context writability and settings.json, but never skills. The user then finds skill-based workflows referenced in docs that simply don't fire, with no error to search for. Note the same run also copies `agents/CLAUDE.md` into `.claude/agents/` (31 files installed from 30 agents + the directory's own CLAUDE.md), which `--verify` then reports as "Agent CLAUDE.md: missing YAML frontmatter".
proposed_fix: Add a skills copy loop to `_cmd_install` mirroring the agents/references loops: iterate `Path(source) / "templates" / "skills"` subdirectories, `mkdir` the matching target under `skills_dir`, copy each file with the same `force or upgrade` semantics, count them, and include `skill_count` in the summary line. Add a skills check to `_verify_install`. Separately, exclude `CLAUDE.md` from the `agents_src.glob("*.md")` and `refs_src.glob("*.md")` loops in both install.py and scripts/install.sh.
test_strategy: Run `baton install --scope project --source <repo>` into a tmp_path and assert that every directory name under `templates/skills/` exists under `<tmp>/.claude/skills/` with a non-empty `SKILL.md`, and that the printed summary reports the skill count. A parity test should assert the set of files produced by `baton install` equals the set produced by `scripts/install.sh` for the same source and scope. A third test asserts `CLAUDE.md` is NOT present in `<tmp>/.claude/agents/`.

title: baton install --verify exits 0 when verification finds issues
evidence: `_verify_install(...) -> None` (install.py:76) accumulates problems into `issues: list[str]` (missing agent files, bad frontmatter, missing references, missing starter templates, unwritable team-context, missing settings.json), then at 119-123 does only `if issues: print(f"\nVerification found {len(issues)} issue(s):"); for issue in issues: print(f"  - {issue}")`. There is no `sys.exit`, and the caller at 296-297 is `if args.verify: _verify_install(...)` — the last statement of the handler. Contrast the sibling `_cmd_verify` for package archives, which correctly ends with `if not result.valid: sys.exit(1)` (install.py:340). Reproduced: `baton install --scope project --source /home/user/agent-baton --verify` printed "Verification found 1 issue(s): - Agent CLAUDE.md: missing YAML frontmatter" and returned rc=0.
why_it_matters: `--verify` exists so an install can be gated in CI or a provisioning script (`docs/cli-reference.md:2262` shows `baton install --scope project --upgrade --verify` as a recommended invocation). Because it always exits 0, `baton install --scope project --upgrade --verify && deploy` proceeds on a broken install: no agents on disk, unparseable frontmatter, or a non-writable team-context all pass the gate. The failure is invisible to any non-interactive consumer, which is exactly the class the repo's guiding principle #5 ("Could this functionality be failing silently?") targets.
proposed_fix: Change `_verify_install` to return `list[str]` (or a bool) and have the caller do `issues = _verify_install(...); if issues: sys.exit(1)` — matching `_cmd_verify`'s existing `sys.exit(1)` convention. Document the exit code in the `baton install` section of docs/cli-reference.md (the doc currently states exit codes for `baton sync --verify` at line 2566 but not for `baton install --verify`).
test_strategy: Install into a tmp_path, then delete every file from `<tmp>/.claude/agents/` and re-run `baton install --scope project --source <repo> --verify`; assert `SystemExit` with code 1 and that stdout contains "Verification found". A companion test must assert a clean install with `--verify` exits 0 and prints "Verification passed".

title: discover_commands() keys modules by basename, silently dropping baton improve-conflicts from the parser
evidence: `discover_commands()` builds `found: dict[str, types.ModuleType]` keyed on the bare module name — `found[sub_info.name] = mod` for subpackage modules (main.py:69) and `found[info.name] = mod` for top-level ones (main.py:73). Two different subpackages contain a module named `conflicts_cmd`: `improve/conflicts_cmd.py:36` registers `subparsers.add_parser("improve-conflicts", ...)` and `release/conflicts_cmd.py:27` registers `subparsers.add_parser("predict-conflicts", ...)`. Because `pkgutil.iter_modules` visits packages alphabetically, `release` overwrites `improve` in `found`, so `improve/conflicts_cmd.register()` is never called. Verified by re-running the discovery loop and collecting duplicates: `COLLISIONS: conflicts_cmd ['agent_baton.cli.commands.improve.conflicts_cmd', 'agent_baton.cli.commands.release.conflicts_cmd']`. Confirmed at the CLI: `baton improve-conflicts list` → `baton: error: argument command: invalid choice: 'improve-conflicts'`, exit 2; `predict-conflicts` is present in `baton --help` and `improve-conflicts` is not.
why_it_matters: An entire documented subsystem surface is unreachable with no signal anywhere. improve/conflicts_cmd.py's own docstring describes it as "L2.4 (bd-362f): velocity-zero CLI surface for the conflict-detection pipeline" backed by `ConflictDetector` and `ConflictStore` — so conflicts get detected and written to the `improvement_conflicts` table but there is no way to list, show, or acknowledge them. Worse, the failure mode is structural: any future command whose module basename matches one in another subpackage will vanish the same way, and the collision is invisible because argparse never sees the duplicate. tests/cli/test_command_discovery.py:29-32 claims to guard exactly this ("every module under cli/commands/ that exposes register() must claim a unique top-level subcommand name") but only asserts `add_parser` didn't raise — it iterates the already-deduplicated `discover_commands()` output, so it passes while the command is missing.
proposed_fix: Key `found` by the fully-qualified module path (`f"{info.name}.{sub_info.name}"`) instead of `sub_info.name`, so every module that exposes `register`/`handler` is registered. Optionally raise a clear error if two modules claim the same subcommand string after registration.
test_strategy: A test that walks `cli/commands/**` with `pkgutil`, collects every module exposing both `register` and `handler`, and asserts `len(discover_commands()) == len(that set)` — i.e. discovery drops nothing. Plus an explicit assertion that `"improve-conflicts"` and `"predict-conflicts"` are both in the built parser's subcommand choices.

title: policy-check misses relative Bash paths, so `echo x > .env` bypasses the block that `Write .env` triggers
evidence: `_extract_paths` (policy_check.py:52-64) handles Bash by keeping only tokens where `if "/" in tok or tok.startswith("./") or tok.startswith("../")` (line 60); everything else is discarded, and the list is capped at 5. Reproduced against the built-in `standard_dev` preset (rule `block_env_files`, pattern `**/.env`): payload `{"tool_name":"Write","tool_input":{"file_path":".env"}}` → deny JSON emitted; payload `{"tool_name":"Bash","tool_input":{"command":"echo LEAK > .env"}}` → no output at all, allowed. The token `.env` contains no `/`, so it is dropped before `PolicyEngine.evaluate()` ever sees it. `comply_record.py:28-48` is a byte-identical copy of the same helper (its docstring says "mirrors policy_check logic"), so the compliance audit log records `file_paths: []` for the same command.
why_it_matters: `.env` in the project root — written from Bash — is the single most likely real-world instance of the exact thing `block_env_files` exists to prevent, and it is the case the hook cannot see. The bypass requires no adversarial intent: an agent writing `echo "KEY=..." >> .env` in cwd is ordinary behavior. The gap is invisible to the operator because the hook emits nothing on allow, and the mirrored bug in comply_record means the audit trail also shows no file touched, so post-hoc review cannot reconstruct it either. The 5-token cap adds a second silent hole for longer commands.
proposed_fix: Extract the shared helper into one module imported by both hooks. Broaden the Bash token filter: keep any token that is not a flag and either contains a path separator OR matches a basename-like pattern (contains a `.` or matches a configured sensitive-name list), and additionally capture redirection targets by scanning for tokens following `>`/`>>`. Raise or remove the 5-token cap. Document the residual limits (shell expansion, variables, heredocs) in the module docstring so operators know the hook is defence-in-depth, not a boundary.
test_strategy: Parametrized tests over the standard_dev preset asserting a deny decision is emitted for each of: `Bash: echo x > .env`, `Bash: cat .env`, `Bash: cp foo .env`, and `Bash: touch a b c d e f secrets/key` (proving the cap does not hide the 6th token) — with the existing `cat /repo/.env` case kept as a regression. A parallel test on `comply-record` must assert the appended JSONL entry's `file_paths` contains `.env` for the same payload.

title: docs/cli-reference.md claims to document every command but omits 31 of 90, including beads, souls, release and handoff
evidence: docs/cli-reference.md:3-4 states: "Complete command reference for the `baton` CLI. Every command, flag, and option is documented here with syntax, defaults, and usage examples." Building the real parser from `discover_commands()` yields 90 distinct top-level subcommands; searching the doc for the literal string `baton <cmd>` finds no occurrence at all for 31 of them: agent-context, aibom, assess, beads, cost-anomalies, daemon-immune, debate, export, finops, forecast, handoff, lookback, maintenance, merge, metrics, overrides, pagerduty, plan-edit, predict-conflicts, quickstart, release, run, slo, souls, storage, tenancy, test-plan, uninstall, users, viz, webhook. `grep -c "baton beads" docs/cli-reference.md` → 0. The doc's own Overview table (lines 17-34) likewise lists no group containing beads, souls, release, tenancy or finops. This violates the stated convention in agent_baton/cli/CLAUDE.md:36-41 ("Adding a command: … 4. Update docs/cli-reference.md").
why_it_matters: `baton beads` is the storage primitive behind the mandatory incident-handling rule and `baton handoff` / `baton release` / `baton merge` are operator-facing workflow commands — a user reading the file the repo advertises as complete (README.md:995 "Full CLI reference", docs/index.md:50 "every `baton` subcommand") has no way to learn their flags, subcommands or exit codes. Because the file asserts completeness, the absence reads as "this command does not exist" rather than "undocumented", so users don't go looking in references/baton-engine.md where some of it actually lives. This is guiding principle #7 ("Does a user have the information needed to use this capability?") failing across a third of the surface.
proposed_fix: Add a reference section for each missing command (syntax block, argument table, exit codes, one example) — prioritising the operator-facing ones: beads, souls, handoff, release, merge, uninstall, storage, viz, tenancy, finops, webhook, run. Until that backlog is closed, soften the line-3 completeness claim and add an explicit "Not yet documented" list so readers know to check `baton <cmd> --help`.
test_strategy: A docs test that builds the parser from `discover_commands()`, collects every top-level subcommand name, and asserts each has a matching heading (`### \`baton <name>\``) in docs/cli-reference.md — failing with the list of missing names. This makes the cli/CLAUDE.md step-4 convention mechanically enforced rather than advisory.

title: Error paths that print "error:" and still exit 0 (pagerduty, uninstall)
evidence: pagerduty_cmd.py:49-54: `if not notifier._routing_key: print("error: no PagerDuty routing key configured.\n  Set BATON_PAGERDUTY_KEY or pass --routing-key KEY."); return` — printed to stdout, not stderr, and the handler returns normally. Reproduced: `baton pagerduty` → prints that line, exit 0. Line 42 does the same for an unknown subcommand: `print(f"Unknown pagerduty sub-command: {args.pd_command}")` then returns 0. Lines 64-67: when `notify_incident` returns `None` the CLI prints "Test event request completed (no dedup_key returned or notifier disabled)." — and `PagerDutyNotifier.notify_incident` (agent_baton/core/observe/pagerduty.py:124-128) returns `None` on any network exception (`except Exception as exc: logger.warning(...); return None`), so a failed POST is reported as "completed". uninstall.py:85-93: the removal loop does `except OSError as exc: print(f"  Failed to remove {name}: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)` and then unconditionally prints "Uninstall complete." and exits 0. Both contradict agent_baton/cli/CLAUDE.md's stated convention ("Errors raise `BatonError` (or subclass) from `errors.py`") and the semantic exit codes defined in agent_baton/cli/errors.py:8-11.
why_it_matters: `baton pagerduty test` is the only way to confirm the alerting integration works, and it cannot fail: unconfigured key, wrong subcommand, and a rejected HTTP POST all produce exit 0. A provisioning script that runs it as a smoke check will green-light an environment where no incident will ever page anyone. `baton uninstall --scope user --yes` reporting "Uninstall complete." with exit 0 after a permission error leaves stale agent definitions on disk while the caller believes the machine is clean — the next `baton install` then merges into a state nobody expects.
proposed_fix: In pagerduty_cmd.py use `from agent_baton.cli.errors import user_error, validation_error`: missing routing key → `user_error("no PagerDuty routing key configured", hint="Set BATON_PAGERDUTY_KEY or pass --routing-key KEY.")`; unknown subcommand → `validation_error(...)`; and have `notify_incident` distinguish "disabled" from "send failed" (e.g. raise or return a status object) so line 67 can `user_error` on a real failure. In uninstall.py, track failures in the loop and `sys.exit(1)` with a "partially removed" summary instead of printing "Uninstall complete."
test_strategy: Assert `baton pagerduty test` with `BATON_PAGERDUTY_KEY` unset raises `SystemExit(1)` and writes the message to stderr (not stdout); assert `baton pagerduty bogus` exits 2. With `notify_incident` monkeypatched to return `None` after a simulated network error, assert exit is non-zero. For uninstall, monkeypatch `shutil.rmtree` to raise `OSError` and assert `SystemExit` with a non-zero code and that stdout does not contain "Uninstall complete."

title: fold_back() can never succeed: git refuses to fetch into a branch checked out in the worktree
evidence:
`create()` makes the worktree branch and checks it out inside the worktree (`_run_git(["switch", "-c", branch_name], cwd=worktree_path)`, worktree_manager.py:565-569). Both fold strategies then try to pull that same ref back into the canonical repo:

    _run_git(["fetch", str(handle.path), f"{handle.branch}:{handle.branch}"], cwd=self._canonical_repo)   # line 693-696 (_rebase_fold), 734-737 (_merge_fold)

Linked worktrees share the ref namespace with the main repo, so `refs/heads/worktree/<task>/<step>` is already present *and checked out in a worktree*. Reproduced on git 2.43.0 in a scratch repo using the real `WorktreeManager`:

    FOLD FAILED: WorktreeFoldError git fetch .../.claude/worktrees/t1/1.1 worktree/t1/1.1:worktree/t1/1.1 failed (exit 128):
    fatal: refusing to fetch into branch 'refs/heads/worktree/t1/1.1' checked out at '.../.claude/worktrees/t1/1.1'

The same failure occurs for `strategy="merge"`. `executor.record_step_result` calls `fold_back(_handle, commit_hash=commit_hash)` with the default `strategy="rebase"` (executor.py:2990-2992), catches `WorktreeFoldError`, and then sets `result.status = "failed"` (line 3012).
why_it_matters: Any step that completes with a recorded commit hash under worktree isolation is flipped from complete to FAILED with `error="WorktreeFoldError: ... refusing to fetch into branch ..."`, and the agent's commits are never integrated into the working branch. The accompanying bead is also misleading: `_parse_conflict_files` finds nothing in the fetch error, so operators see `worktree-fold-conflict step=1.1 files=[]` and are pointed at a merge conflict that does not exist. The only passing fold tests use `strategy="none"` (tests/test_worktree_manager.py:242-289) or assert that rebase *raises* (line 301-336) — that test passes for the wrong reason, so the defect is invisible to CI.
proposed_fix: Delete both `git fetch <worktree-path> <branch>:<branch>` calls — the ref is already visible in the canonical repo because worktrees share `.git`. Perform the rebase with an explicit non-checked-out target (e.g. `git rebase --onto <base_branch> <base_sha> <sha>` writing to a temp ref, or run the rebase inside the worktree where the branch IS checked out) and then integrate with a real working-tree-updating command in the canonical repo (`git merge --ff-only <branch>` / `git merge --no-ff <branch>`), not a bare ref write.
test_strategy: Add a real-git test (no mocks) that creates a worktree, commits a file inside it, advances the parent branch with a non-conflicting commit, calls `fold_back(handle, commit_hash=<sha>)` with the DEFAULT strategy, and asserts (a) no exception is raised, (b) `git show <base_branch>:<agent-file>` succeeds in the canonical repo, and (c) `git status --porcelain` in the canonical repo is empty. Also assert `WorktreeFoldError.conflict_files` is non-empty in the genuine-conflict test so it can no longer pass on a fetch refusal.

title: Fold-back writes the parent branch ref with update-ref while it is checked out, silently staging a revert of the agent's work
evidence:
`_fast_forward` and step 4 of `_rebase_fold` move the parent branch with a plumbing ref write executed from the canonical repo, where that branch is normally the checked-out branch:

    _run_git(["update-ref", f"refs/heads/{handle.base_branch}", commit_hash], cwd=self._canonical_repo)   # line 761-764

`update-ref` does not touch the index or working tree. Reproduced with the real manager (`strategy="none"` after an agent commit in the worktree):

    none -> edcc63c8...
    ## main
    D  agent.txt          <-- staged deletion of the file that was just "folded in"
    files in parent worktree: ['.claude', '.git']

The branch now contains `agent.txt`, but the parent working tree does not, and the deletion is already staged.
why_it_matters: After a fold the parent repo is left with the agent's files staged for deletion. The orchestrator's next `git commit` (CLAUDE.md mandates committing each agent's work individually) silently commits the revert, erasing the folded work while the trace records a successful `worktree_fold`. This is the same class of parent-HEAD drift the root CLAUDE.md warns about, produced by baton itself.
proposed_fix: Never advance a branch that may be checked out with `update-ref`. Integrate from the canonical repo with `git merge --ff-only <worktree-branch>` (or `git merge --no-ff`) so the index and working tree move with the ref; if the base branch is genuinely not checked out anywhere (verify with `git worktree list --porcelain`), `update-ref` is acceptable but should be gated on that check.
test_strategy: After a successful `fold_back` on a repo whose canonical checkout is on `base_branch`, assert `git status --porcelain` in the canonical repo returns empty output AND the agent's file exists on disk in the parent working tree — today the same assertion yields `D agent.txt` and a missing file.

title: Agent commits made inside a worktree are invisible to the launcher, so the engine deletes the worktree and force-deletes its branch
evidence:
`launch()` accepts `cwd_override` (the worktree path) and runs the agent subprocess there (`cwd = cwd_override or str(self._config.working_directory ...)`, line 523), but the git probes ignore it:

    async def _git_rev_parse(self) -> str:
        proc = await asyncio.create_subprocess_exec(
            self._git_bin, "rev-parse", "HEAD", ...,
            cwd=str(self._config.working_directory or Path.cwd()),   # line 904 — parent repo, NOT the worktree
        )

and `result.commit_hash` is only set when `post_commit != pre_commit` (line 564-567). Both reads hit the parent repo, which the isolated agent by construction never advances, so `commit_hash` stays `""` and `files_changed` stays `[]`. `record_step_result` then takes the `else` branch at executor.py:3037 ("No commit: clean up without fold") and calls `cleanup(_handle, on_failure=False)` → `_do_cleanup` runs `git worktree remove` and then `subprocess.run(["git", "branch", "-D", handle.branch], ...)` (worktree_manager.py:896-900). The existing launcher tests set `launcher._git_bin = None` (tests/test_claude_launcher.py:1031, 1063) so this path is never exercised.
why_it_matters: A specialist that does exactly what the Worktree Discipline block tells it to do — commit inside its worktree — has its work force-deleted: the worktree directory is removed and the branch holding the commits is destroyed with `branch -D`, leaving the commits unreachable. The step is recorded `complete` with `files_changed=[]`, so the loss is invisible in the trace and in the retrospective; the only symptom is `INCONCLUSIVE step ...: no files_changed and no commit_hash recorded` (execute.py:1741).
proposed_fix: Thread `cwd_override` into `_git_rev_parse`/`_git_diff_files` (pass the effective `cwd` used for the subprocess) so pre/post HEAD are read from the worktree the agent actually ran in. Additionally harden `record_step_result`: before taking the no-commit cleanup branch, re-read HEAD in `handle.path` and compare against `handle.base_sha`; refuse to delete a worktree whose HEAD is ahead of its base.
test_strategy: Launch with `cwd_override=<worktree>` against a real git repo where the fake agent creates a commit inside the worktree only, and assert `LaunchResult.commit_hash` equals the worktree HEAD and `files_changed` lists the worktree file. Separately, assert `record_step_result(status="complete", commit_hash="")` does NOT call cleanup when `git rev-parse HEAD` in the worktree differs from `handle.base_sha`.

title: gc_stale's in-flight guard queries a column that does not exist, so both safety gates are inert and live worktrees can be force-deleted
evidence:
`_is_in_flight` runs:

    rows = _conn.execute("SELECT task_id, state_json FROM executions WHERE status = 'running'").fetchall()

inside a `try:` whose handler is `except Exception: pass` (line 992-993). The production `executions` table has no `state_json` column — verified by building the real schema and dumping it:

    executions columns: ['task_id','status','current_phase','current_step_index','started_at','completed_at','created_at','updated_at','pending_gaps','resolved_decisions','force_override','override_justification','run_cumulative_spend_usd','scope_expansions_applied','working_branch','working_branch_head','consolidation_result_json','pending_scope_expansions_json','pending_approval_request_json','phase_retries_json','version']
    has state_json: False
    _is_in_flight -> (False, '')

(worktree paths actually live in a separate `step_worktrees` table, schema.py:1237.) The only test that covers this creates its own fake table — `CREATE TABLE executions (task_id TEXT, status TEXT, state_json TEXT)` (tests/test_worktree_manager.py:1142) — so it passes against a schema that does not exist. The second gate is equally dead: `terminal_step_ids` is referenced nowhere outside worktree_manager.py, and both production call sites (`executor.py:681-684` engine-init daemon thread, `executor.py:4387` on execute-complete) pass nothing, so the docstring's "SAFETY: never deletes a worktree whose step is still in running, dispatched, interacting, or gate_pending" (line 1005-1007) never applies.
why_it_matters: Every `ExecutionEngine` construction spawns a background `gc_stale()` thread. With both guards inert and the default age now 4h (`_get_default_stale_hours`, line 935), any `baton` command force-removes every worktree older than 4 hours — including the worktree of a step still being worked on in a long-running run, and including a failed worktree retained for developer takeover (the execution's status is then `paused-takeover`/`failed`, which would not have matched `status='running'` anyway). `_do_cleanup(force=True)` runs `git worktree remove --force` and `git branch -D`, so an in-progress or under-takeover developer's commits are destroyed with no recoverable ref. The user-facing numbers also drift: takeover.py:212 says "GC'd (72h default)", docs/pillars/right-agent-right-time.md:82 says 72 hours, and `baton execute worktree-gc` defaults to 72 (execute.py:406-410), while the engine's automatic GC uses 4.
proposed_fix: Rewrite `_is_in_flight` to join the real schema: `SELECT e.task_id FROM step_worktrees w JOIN executions e USING(task_id) WHERE w.worktree_path = ? AND e.status IN ('running','queued','paused-takeover','approval_pending','gate_failed')`. Replace the blanket `except Exception: pass` with a logged handler plus fail-safe `return (True, "unknown")` so an unreadable DB blocks deletion rather than authorising it. Have both engine call sites pass `terminal_step_ids` computed from `state.completed_step_ids | state.failed_step_ids`, and reconcile the 4h/72h documentation with the code.
test_strategy: Build the DB from the real `PROJECT_SCHEMA_DDL`, insert a `running` execution plus its `step_worktrees` row, backdate the manifest past the threshold, and assert `gc_stale()` returns [] and the directory still exists. Add a second test asserting that when the DB query raises, `_is_in_flight` returns True (fail-safe) and the worktree survives. Add a static assertion that `executions` has every column `_is_in_flight` selects.

title: ExecutionAction.worktree_path is never populated, so the documented orchestrator contract silently bypasses isolation
evidence: `ExecutionAction` defines `worktree_path` / `worktree_branch` (models/execution.py:1957-1958) and `to_dict()` emits them when non-empty (1991-1994); `_print_action` prints `Worktree:` / `Branch:` when present (execute.py:672-675). But a repo-wide grep shows nothing ever assigns them — `_dispatch_action`'s `return ExecutionAction(...)` (executor.py:7208-7221) and `_team_dispatch_action`'s member actions (7938-7944) omit both fields. The worktree is only created later, inside `mark_dispatched` (executor.py:3195-3256), and `baton execute dispatched` prints only `{"status": "dispatched", "step_id": ...}` (execute.py:1073-1074). Meanwhile `agents/orchestrator.md:68-72` instructs: "When the action also carries a `worktree_path` field, pass that path as the `cwd` parameter on the `Agent(...)` invocation ... Without this, the agent boots in the parent project root and the worktree isolation is silently bypassed." The only tests construct `ExecutionAction(worktree_path="/some/path")` by hand (tests/test_worktree_manager.py:669-716) — they assert the dataclass, never the engine behaviour.
why_it_matters: In the orchestrator-driven protocol (the flow `agents/orchestrator.md` documents), the field never appears, so the orchestrator spawns every specialist in the parent project root. Parallel agents then share one working tree — exactly the cross-agent overwrite the CLAUDE.md concurrency rule exists to prevent — while the engine believes each step ran isolated and later attempts a fold-back of an empty worktree. Only the `baton execute run` path escapes this, because the CLI re-reads the path from `state.step_worktrees` itself (execute.py:2642-2652).
proposed_fix: Either (a) allocate the worktree during `next_action()`/`_dispatch_action` and populate `action.worktree_path`/`worktree_branch` from the handle, or (b) keep allocation in `mark_dispatched` and make `baton execute dispatched` return `{"worktree_path": ..., "worktree_branch": ...}` in its JSON, updating `agents/orchestrator.md` and `references/baton-engine.md` to read it from there. Same treatment is needed for team-member actions, which currently get `isolation="worktree"` (executor.py:7994-7999) with no path at all.
test_strategy: Drive the engine to a DISPATCH for a non-automation step with worktrees enabled and assert `action.to_dict()["worktree_path"]` equals the created handle path and that `_print_action` renders a `Worktree:` line; and assert the JSON emitted by `baton execute dispatched` contains the worktree path for that step.

title: InteractiveDecisionManager raises UnboundLocalError on EOF instead of rejecting the gate
evidence:
The EOF branch sets `choice` and `feedback` but never `chosen`, then breaks straight into the constructor that reads `chosen`:

    except EOFError:
        choice = "reject"
        feedback = "Aborted via EOF"
        break
    ...
    self._resolutions[req.request_id] = DecisionResolution(..., chosen_option=chosen, feedback=feedback)

Reproduced by calling `InteractiveDecisionManager(decisions_dir=tmp).request(req)` with stdin at `/dev/null`:

    File ".../agent_baton/core/orchestration/runner.py", line 67, in request
        chosen_option=chosen,
    UnboundLocalError: cannot access local variable 'chosen' where it is not associated with a value
why_it_matters: `BatonRunner` force-installs this decision manager on the worker (runner.py:100-110), and EOF is the normal state for every non-TTY run — CI, `nohup`, a daemonized `baton` loop, or a session driven by an agent. Instead of recording a clean `reject` and unwinding, the approval gate crashes the run loop with an unhandled UnboundLocalError, losing the in-flight execution rather than pausing it.
proposed_fix: Set `chosen = "reject"` in the `except EOFError` branch (and drop the now-unused `choice` assignment), or better, detect `not sys.stdin.isatty()` in `__init__` and fall back to the file-based `DecisionManager.request()` so headless runs use the documented out-of-band approval flow instead of failing.
test_strategy: Call `InteractiveDecisionManager.request()` with stdin patched to raise `EOFError` and assert it returns normally with `get(request_id).chosen_option == "reject"` and a non-empty feedback string — today it raises UnboundLocalError.

title: TeamMailbox.append performs no locking and derives event_id from a racy read-then-write, contradicting its own docstring
evidence:
The module docstring claims "each enqueue takes a brief `filelock`-style sentinel via atomic rename to avoid interleaved partial writes from concurrent dispatchers" (lines 11-13) and `append()`'s own docstring claims "writes go to a temp file in the same directory and are then atomically appended via a short open(...; \"a\") in one `os.fsync`-bounded call" (lines 166-170). The implementation does none of that — no lock, no temp file, no rename, no fsync (the `tempfile`/`os` imports at lines 37-38 are unused):

    existing = self._count_existing()
    event = MailboxEvent(..., event_id=f"e{existing + 1}", ...)
    with open(self._path, "a", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        fh.write(line)
why_it_matters: The mailbox is written from the executor's per-member dispatch loop (executor.py:7947-7970) and, under the claude-teams backend, from independent `baton execute team-record` hook processes fired per teammate (team_backends.py:334-347) — genuinely concurrent writers. Two appends that interleave between `_count_existing()` and `write()` both mint the same `event_id`, and `read_since(after_event_id)` resolves an id by first match (mailbox.py:239-243), so a reader draining incrementally silently replays or skips every event between the duplicates. Because the docstring asserts a locking scheme that does not exist, a maintainer auditing the concurrency story will conclude it is safe.
proposed_fix: Make ids collision-proof (monotonic counter in a sidecar file guarded by `fcntl.flock`, or a ULID/uuid4 `event_id` with ordering carried by `timestamp` + file order) and either implement the advertised `flock` around append or rewrite both docstrings to state the actual guarantee. Drop the unused `tempfile`/`os` imports.
test_strategy: Spawn N threads/processes each calling `append()` once on the same mailbox and assert `len({e.event_id for e in read_all()}) == N` and `len(read_all()) == N`; then assert `read_since(<id of event k>)` returns exactly the N-k later events.

title: First bead write silently rewrites the user's tracked .gitignore and git-ignores baton.db
evidence:
`BdClient.init()` docstring at bd_client.py:116-134 claims the flags neutralise bd's onboarding: "``--setup-exclude``— keep ``.beads/`` local via ``.git/info/exclude`` (untracked) instead of editing the project's ``.gitignore``" and "baton owns those surfaces, so we suppress all of it". `BdBeadStore._ensure_init()` (bd_bead_store.py:65-68) calls this lazily on the first `write`/`close`/`annotate`/`link`.

I reproduced against the installed `bd version 1.2.1` in a scratch git repo with a pre-existing committed `.gitignore` containing only `node_modules/`. A single `make_bead_store(...).write(bead)` produced:

```
=== git status ===
 M .gitignore
=== gitignore ===
node_modules/

# Beads / Dolt files (added by bd init)
.dolt/
*.db
.beads-credential-key
.beads/proxieddb/
*.gate.lock*
```

and then:

```
$ git check-ignore -v .claude/team-context/baton.db
.gitignore:5:*.db	.claude/team-context/baton.db
```

`--setup-exclude` does add `.beads/` to `.git/info/exclude`, but bd *also* appends the block above to the tracked `.gitignore` regardless. No code path in baton checks for or reverts this.
why_it_matters: On the very first bead write in any user project (i.e. the first dispatched step of the first `baton execute` run), baton mutates a tracked file it explicitly promised not to touch. Two concrete failures: (1) the root CLAUDE.md orchestrator protocol says "commit each agent's work individually" — the stray `.gitignore` diff gets swept into the specialist's commit and lands in the user's PR with no explanation; (2) the appended `*.db` rule is broad enough to match `.claude/team-context/baton.db`, so a user who previously tracked baton state (or any `*.db` fixture — SQLite test fixtures, seed databases) silently stops seeing them in `git status`/`git add`. Worktree-isolated parallel specialists each hit this in their own worktree, producing conflicting `.gitignore` edits.
proposed_fix: After `self._run(["init", ...])` in `BdClient.init()`, detect and revert the damage rather than trusting the flag. Concretely: snapshot `(repo_root/'.gitignore')` bytes (or its absence) before the `bd init` subprocess, and restore it afterwards, migrating any bd-added patterns into `.git/info/exclude` instead. Log at INFO what was moved. Alternatively run `bd init` with `cwd` pointing at a baton-owned subdirectory that is not the git root, so bd has no tracked `.gitignore` to edit. Either way, add an explicit post-init assertion that `git diff --name-only` is empty for `.gitignore`, and downgrade the docstring claim to describe what is actually enforced.
test_strategy: Integration test gated on `shutil.which('bd')`: create a tmp git repo, commit a `.gitignore` with a known sentinel line, run `make_bead_store(db, repo_root=tmp).write(sample_bead)`, then assert (a) `(tmp/'.gitignore').read_text()` is byte-identical to the committed content, (b) `subprocess.run(['git','status','--porcelain','.gitignore'])` produces empty stdout, and (c) `git check-ignore .claude/team-context/baton.db` exits non-zero. A unit-level companion can monkeypatch `BdClient._run` to simulate bd appending to `.gitignore` and assert `init()` restores it.

title: `baton beads cleanup` memory decay is a hard-coded no-op while its dry-run reports a non-zero count
evidence:
`BdBeadStore.decay()` (bd_bead_store.py:258-267) is: `_log.debug("BdBeadStore.decay is a no-op (bd owns compaction); returning 0"); return 0`. It is the only bead store implementation (`bead_backend.make_bead_store` always returns `BdBeadStore`, bead_backend.py:41-78).

`decay_beads()` (bead_decay.py:58-65) takes two divergent paths: `if dry_run: return _count_eligible(...)` — which does a real `bead_store.query(status='closed')` scan — else `return bead_store.decay(...)`, i.e. always 0. The CLI (bead_cmd.py:824-833) prints those two numbers with identical framing.

Live repro against real `bd 1.2.1` with two closed beads present:
```
DRY  ttl=0 -> 2
REAL ttl=0 -> 0
statuses after: [('bd-t001','closed'), ('bd-t002','archived'), ('bd-old1','closed')]
```
So `baton beads cleanup --dry-run` prints "Dry run: 2 bead(s) would be archived" and the real command prints "Archived 0 bead(s)" and changes nothing.

The capability is still documented as working: README.md:628 `baton beads cleanup --ttl 168 --dry-run    # Memory decay preview`; README.md:821 "Archive old closed beads (memory decay)"; references/baton-engine.md:906-916 documents `--ttl`/`--task`/`--dry-run` with no caveat; bead_decay.py:11-13 still promises "their verbose ``content`` is replaced by a compact archival marker, freeing context budget for future agents". `executor.py:4584-4596` calls `decay_beads` on completion and logs "Bead decay: archived %d bead(s)" — always 0.
why_it_matters: An operator running `baton beads cleanup --ttl 168 --dry-run` on a long-lived project is told N beads will be archived, runs it for real, is told 0, and has no way to tell whether that is a bug or means the beads aged out between the two calls. Nothing ever compacts bead content, so `BeadSelector.select()` (bead_selector.py:192, `query(status='open', limit=500)`) keeps pulling full-fat historical beads into every dispatch prompt for the life of the project — the exact context-budget bloat decay existed to prevent. There is no operator-visible signal: the no-op logs at DEBUG.
proposed_fix: Implement `BdBeadStore.decay()` for real: query closed beads (`status='closed'`), filter by parsed `closed_at` older than `max_age_days` (parse with `datetime.fromisoformat`, not the string comparison in `_count_eligible`), and for each set `bead.status='archived'` and `bead.content` to a compact marker, then `write(bead)` (which already round-trips `baton-status:archived` via `bead_labels`, bd_mapping.py:79-80 — I verified archived status survives the round trip). If the team genuinely wants bd to own compaction, then delete the CLI verb, the `decay_beads` helper, and the executor hook, and remove the README/`references/baton-engine.md` entries — do not ship a command that prints a fabricated dry-run number.
test_strategy: A test must assert dry-run/real-run agreement, not just the no-op contract that tests/test_bead_tiers234.py:370-393 currently locks in. Write N closed beads with `closed_at` older than the TTL, then assert `decay_beads(store, ttl_hours=T, dry_run=True) == decay_beads(store, ttl_hours=T, dry_run=False)` and that afterwards `store.read(bid).status == 'archived'` and `len(store.read(bid).content) < len(original_content)` for each. Add a second assertion that a bead closed *inside* the TTL window is untouched.

title: F11 bead conflict detection is dead: `contradicts` links never produce the `conflict:unresolved` tag the detector looks for
evidence:
`_LINK_TO_BD_DEP` (bd_bead_store.py:38-46) maps `"contradicts": "related"`. `BdBeadStore.link()` (bd_bead_store.py:125-131) does only `self._bd.dep_add(source_id, target_id, ...)` — no tagging. `write()` (bd_bead_store.py:95-100) does the same for beads carrying `links`.

`has_unresolved_conflicts()` (bd_bead_store.py:236-244) looks for exactly one thing: `self.query(task_id=task_id, status="open", tags=["conflict:unresolved"])`.

A repo-wide grep for `conflict:unresolved` finds writers only in tests and in `bead_cmd.py`'s *display* code — nothing in production ever applies the tag. The deleted SQLite store did: `git show 55f30e7^:agent_baton/core/engine/bead_store.py` shows `link()` at :697 with "# F11 — conflict detection: tag both beads when a conflict link is created" calling `self._add_conflict_tag(conn, source_id)` / `(conn, target_id)` at :737-740.

The consumer is live: `executor.py:6362-6373` calls `has_unresolved_conflicts(state.task_id)` on every resolver loop and, on True, logs a warning and publishes a `bead_conflict` domain event. The producer is live too: `core/exec/runner.py:237` sets `link_type = "validates" if result.exit_code == 0 else "contradicts"` and attaches it as a `BeadLink` on the child result bead (runner.py:271-283) whenever an executable bead's script fails.

The test suite documents rather than catches this — tests/test_bead_tiers234.py:795-806: "BdBeadStore.link() creates a bd dependency but does NOT add the conflict:unresolved tag ... Tests are retargeted: write beads with conflict:unresolved in their tags list directly".
why_it_matters: A failing executable bead creates a `contradicts` edge to its parent — the canonical "this recorded knowledge is now falsified" signal. Under the bd backend that edge becomes an untyped `related` dependency, `has_unresolved_conflicts` returns False forever, the executor's F11 warning never fires, and no `bead_conflict` event reaches the event bus / learn pipeline. Downstream agents then keep receiving the falsified parent bead from `BeadSelector` with no contradiction marker. This is precisely the repo's own guiding-principle-5 failure: a governance signal that fails silently and whose tests were rewritten to assert the broken behaviour.
proposed_fix: In `BdBeadStore.link()` and in the `for link in bead.links` loop of `write()` (bd_bead_store.py:95-100), when `link_type == "contradicts"`, add `conflict:unresolved` to both endpoints' tags via a read-modify-`write` (the label set is already recomputed from `bead.tags` by `bead_labels`, bd_mapping.py:65-88, so the tag becomes a queryable bd label automatically — I confirmed tags survive as labels). Keep it best-effort/`BdError`-guarded like the existing dep_add. `resolve_conflict()` (bd_bead_store.py:246-256) already removes the tag correctly, so the pair becomes symmetric.
test_strategy: Test the *producer→detector* path end to end, not the tag in isolation: write parent bead P and child bead C, call `store.link(C.bead_id, P.bead_id, 'contradicts')`, then assert `store.has_unresolved_conflicts(task_id) is True` and that both `store.read(C.bead_id).tags` and `store.read(P.bead_id).tags` contain `conflict:unresolved`. Add a negative case asserting `link(..., 'validates')` leaves `has_unresolved_conflicts` False. Also add an `ExecutableBeadRunner` test: run a script with a non-zero exit code against a real store and assert `has_unresolved_conflicts` flips True.

title: Bead IDs collide across tasks and the colliding write silently overwrites another task's bead
evidence:
`_generate_bead_id` (models/bead.py:63-99) scales ID length off `bead_count`, documented as "Current total number of beads in the project": `<500 → 4 hex chars (~65k namespace)`. Every production call site passes a **task-scoped** count instead: executor.py:2570 `len(self._bead_store.query(task_id=state.task_id, limit=10000))`, likewise executor.py:2667, executor.py:5174, executor.py:5406, executor.py:1445. `exec/runner.py:244` skips the helper entirely: `child_bead_id = f"bd-{child_sha[:4]}"` — permanently 4 chars.

The bd namespace, however, is project-global (one `.beads/` at repo root shared by every task), so IDs never lengthen no matter how large the project gets. Simulating 20 tasks x 100 beads (2000 project beads, per-task count always <500):
```
total beads 2000  distinct ids 1975  cross-task collisions 23
CROSS-TASK COLLISION bd-d7ce ('T-0','0.84') <-> ('T-4','4.46')
```

`BdBeadStore.write()` (bd_bead_store.py:78-93) resolves a collision by *taking the update branch*: `existing = self._bd.show(bead.bead_id)`; when non-None it issues `self._bd.update(bead_id, status=..., set_labels=bead_labels(bead), metadata={"baton": bead.to_dict()})` — replacing the whole metadata blob and the whole label set. Live repro against real bd:
```
write  Bead(bd-cccc, task=T-A, agent=architect, type=decision, 'Task A: use RS256')
write  Bead(bd-cccc, task=T-B, agent=qa,        type=warning,  'Task B: flaky test')
read   -> T-B 9.9 qa warning 'Task B: flaky test'
```
Task A's decision bead is gone, with no error and no log line — `write()` returns the bead_id as if it succeeded.
why_it_matters: In any repo that runs baton for more than a handful of tasks, a new task's warning bead can annihilate an earlier task's architectural decision bead. The loss is invisible: `write()` returns a truthy id, no exception, no warning. Downstream, `BeadSelector` and knowledge-gap auto-resolution (`knowledge_gap._resolve_from_beads`, knowledge_gap.py:237, which queries across all tasks) surface the surviving bead under the destroyed one's identity. This is memory corruption in the subsystem whose entire purpose is durable cross-step memory.
proposed_fix: Two changes. (1) Make the ID length reflect the real namespace: have call sites pass a project-global count (`bead_store.query(limit=...)` without `task_id`, or better, a cheap `count()` method on the store backed by `bd list --json | len`) — or drop the progressive scaling and use a fixed 8+ hex chars, which the `bd-[0-9a-f]+` feedback regex in bead_signal.py:78 already accepts. Fix `exec/runner.py:244` to use `_generate_bead_id` rather than a hard-coded 4-char slice. (2) Make collisions non-silent: in `BdBeadStore.write()`, when `existing` is found, compare the existing blob's `(task_id, step_id, created_at)` against the incoming bead; on mismatch, log a warning and retry `create` with a longer/suffixed id instead of clobbering.
test_strategy: Two assertions. Collision-safety: write bead A `(bead_id='bd-cccc', task_id='T-A', content='A')`, then bead B `(bead_id='bd-cccc', task_id='T-B', content='B')`; assert `store.read('bd-cccc').task_id == 'T-A'` (original preserved) and that B was persisted under a *different* id that `store.query(task_id='T-B')` returns. Namespace: assert `_generate_bead_id(..., bead_count=2000)` yields more than 4 hex chars, and add a property test over 5000 synthetic (task_id, step_id, content) triples asserting zero duplicate ids.

title: `BdBeadStore.close(summary=...)` discards the summary and bd overwrites the bead's recorded closed_at
evidence:
`close()` (bd_bead_store.py:106-114) writes the summary only as a bd note plus a close `--reason`; it never updates the `metadata.baton` blob. `bd_issue_to_bead` (bd_mapping.py:110-136) prefers that blob for every field except `status`/`closed_at`, so `bead.summary` reads back as whatever it was at create time — empty.

Live repro:
```
store.close('bd-t001', 'done: verified')
read -> status closed  closed_at '2026-08-14T03:19:47Z'  summary ''
```
And for a bead written with its own `closed_at='2026-01-02T00:00:00Z'`:
```
archived read status: archived  closed_at '2026-08-14T03:19:48Z'
```
bd's stamp replaces baton's recorded timestamp (bd_mapping.py:134-135 `if issue.get("closed_at"): bead.closed_at = str(issue["closed_at"])`).

The model still documents the field as populated: models/bead.py:173 "summary: Compacted description (populated on close or decay)." Live consumers render it: `core/release/mrp.py:212` and `:246` build the Merge Readiness Package's "Beads Filed" and "Outstanding Follow-ups" tables from `(b.summary or "")`; `api/routes/pmo_h3.py:580` returns `summary=b.summary or ""` to the PMO UI; `cli/commands/observe/export.py:225` exports `"summary": b.summary`. The executor's terminal-closure path (executor.py:5741) passes real summaries ("Plan execution completed" / "Task failed before bead was closed") that are all dropped.
why_it_matters: Every reviewer-facing surface that renders bead summaries now shows a blank column. The MRP is explicitly a human review artifact — a reviewer opening "Outstanding Follow-ups" sees bead ids and types with no explanation of what happened, and there is no error to tell them the data was lost rather than never recorded. Separately, the `closed_at` overwrite means baton can no longer distinguish when a bead was *actually* closed from when bd was told about it, which is exactly the timestamp any real decay/TTL implementation must key off (see the decay finding).
proposed_fix: In `close()`, read the bead, set `bead.summary = summary` and `bead.status = 'closed'` (and `bead.closed_at` if not already set), then `self._bd.update(bead_id, metadata={'baton': bead.to_dict()})` before calling `self._bd.close(...)` — the same read-modify-write pattern already used by `update_quality_score` (bd_bead_store.py:206-220). In `bd_issue_to_bead`, only overlay bd's `closed_at` when the blob's own `closed_at` is empty, so a baton-recorded close time wins.
test_strategy: Assert round-trip persistence, not just the bd side-effects: `store.write(b); store.close(b.bead_id, 'compacted summary text')`, then `store.read(b.bead_id)` must have `.summary == 'compacted summary text'` and `.status == 'closed'`. Separately, write a bead with an explicit `closed_at='2025-01-01T00:00:00Z'` and `status='closed'` and assert `store.read(...).closed_at == '2025-01-01T00:00:00Z'` (bd's stamp must not clobber it). Add an MRP-level test asserting the "Beads Filed" table row for a closed bead contains the summary text.

title: `BATON_BD_BACKEND` / `BATON_BD_ENABLED` are documented as live but their implementations are dead code
evidence:
Root CLAUDE.md:141 documents: "`BATON_BD_BACKEND` — ... Any other value logs a deprecation warning and raises `BdNotAvailable` if `bd` binary is missing." `selected_backend()` (bead_backend.py:24-38) is the only code that reads `BATON_BD_BACKEND` and does emit that warning — but `make_bead_store()` (bead_backend.py:41-78), the single construction path used by all 15+ call sites (`api/deps.py:149`, `api/routes/pmo_h3.py:326`, `cli/commands/bead_cmd.py:109`, `core/storage/central.py:488`, …), never calls it. Repo-wide grep for `selected_backend` returns only `bead_backend.py` itself and `tests/test_bd_backend.py:19,273`.

Same for `bd_enabled()` (bd_client.py:62-66), whose own module docstring at bd_client.py:25 advertises "``BATON_BD_ENABLED`` — master switch for the beads backend (default ``1``)". Grep for `bd_enabled` returns only its definition and `tests/test_bd_backend.py:13,287-291`.
why_it_matters: A user who followed the previous docs and still has `BATON_BD_BACKEND=sqlite` or `BATON_BD_ENABLED=0` exported in their shell/CI gets zero feedback: no deprecation warning (the warning function is never invoked) and no behavioural difference (bd is used unconditionally). They will reasonably believe their setting is in effect. The stated contract — "logs a deprecation warning" — is measurably false at runtime, and `selected_backend`/`bd_enabled` are dead code kept alive only by their own tests, which is precisely the "tests assert the shape, not the behaviour" smell.
proposed_fix: Call `selected_backend()` at the top of `make_bead_store()` so the deprecation warning actually reaches users with stale settings (its return value is discarded — that is fine, the side effect is the point). Either delete `bd_enabled()` and strike `BATON_BD_ENABLED` from bd_client.py's docstring and the CLAUDE.md/GEMINI.md env tables, or wire it into `make_bead_store` as a documented hard-fail (`BATON_BD_ENABLED=0` → raise a typed error explaining bd is mandatory). title: Cross-project bead projection drops the exact columns `v_cross_project_discoveries` exposes
evidence:
`export_beads_to_central` (central.py:529-556) upserts nine columns only: `(project_id, bead_id, bead_type, status, agent_name, created_at, task_id, step_id, content)` via `INSERT OR REPLACE INTO beads`. Everything else falls to the DDL defaults declared a few lines above at central.py:510-522 — `confidence TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'medium'`, `tags TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]'`, `affected_files TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]'`, `quality_score REAL NOT NULL DEFAULT 0.0`, `retrieval_count INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0`.

The analytics view built on that table selects precisely those dropped columns (schema.py:3477-3484):
```sql
CREATE VIEW IF NOT EXISTS v_cross_project_discoveries AS
SELECT b.project_id, b.bead_id, b.bead_type, b.agent_name, b.content,
       b.confidence, b.tags, b.affected_files, b.created_at,
       b.quality_score, b.retrieval_count, p.task_summary ...
```
Because the upsert is `INSERT OR REPLACE`, each sync also resets any richer values a previous schema version had written. Separately the docstring at central.py:440 says "Reads **open** beads from the project's bead store" but the call is `store.query(limit=50000)` with no `status`, which `BdBeadStore.query` routes to `include_closed=True` (bd_bead_store.py:180) — I confirmed a closed bead is returned by a bare `query()`.
why_it_matters: Anyone querying `v_cross_project_discoveries` — the documented cross-project intelligence surface (docs/architecture/high-level-design.md:214) — gets a table where `confidence` is uniformly 'medium', `tags` and `affected_files` are uniformly empty, and `quality_score`/`retrieval_count` are uniformly 0. A cross-project query like "show me high-confidence discoveries about auth" silently returns nothing (no tag ever matches) or everything (every row reads 'medium'), with no indication the columns are placeholders. The BEAD_FEEDBACK quality signal that `update_quality_score` carefully persists per-project (bd_bead_store.py:206-220) is discarded at the exact point it would become cross-project value.
proposed_fix: Widen the INSERT to carry the full projection: add `confidence, scope, tags (json.dumps(b.tags)), affected_files (json.dumps(...)), closed_at, summary, source, token_estimate, quality_score, retrieval_count` — the DDL columns already exist at central.py:510-522, only the VALUES tuple is short. Fix the docstring at central.py:440 to say all beads (or pass `status='open'` if open-only was the intent). If the projection is deliberately minimal, then drop the unpopulated columns from `v_cross_project_discoveries` rather than exposing constant-valued fields as if they were data.
test_strategy: Write a bead with `confidence='high'`, `tags=['auth','security']`, `affected_files=['auth.py']`, `quality_score=1.5` into a bd-backed project store; run `export_beads_to_central(project_id, root, central_db)`; then `SELECT confidence, tags, affected_files, quality_score FROM v_cross_project_discoveries WHERE bead_id=?` and assert the round-tripped values equal the originals (tags/affected_files parsed back from JSON). Add a second assertion that re-running the export does not reset those columns to defaults.

title: Team-mode self-approval control is bypassed by any caller that omits the identity header
evidence:
`UserIdentityMiddleware._resolve_user_id` documents its third branch as `3. ``"local-user"`` fallback (local mode only)` (user_identity.py:80-84) but the code returns it unconditionally regardless of `self.approval_mode`:

    # 3. Local-mode fallback.
    return "local-user"          # user_identity.py:101

The route's only defence is an identity *inequality* check (spec_queue.py:235-243):

    approval_mode: str = getattr(request.state, "approval_mode", "local")
    if approval_mode == "team" and actor == draft.submitted_by:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=403, ...)

Demonstrated end-to-end with `BATON_APPROVAL_MODE=team` set before process start:

    self-approve as alice (X-Baton-User: alice):   403   # control works
    approve with NO identity header at all:        200 approved   # control bypassed

`TokenAuthMiddleware` is a documented no-op when no token is configured (auth.py:42-57), which is the default for `baton serve`, so the second request needs no credentials at all. The existing test cannot catch this — tests/api/test_specs_api.py:233 asserts `assert r.status_code in (200, 403)`, a tautology that passes whether or not the control fires (and in fact always takes the 200 branch, because `_APPROVAL_MODE` at user_identity.py:35 is read once at import time and the test's `monkeypatch.setenv` runs after import).
why_it_matters: `core/govern/CLAUDE.md:25` states "**`BATON_APPROVAL_MODE=team`** disables self-approval — the approver must differ from the actor. Don't add code that special-cases this away." A deployment that sets `BATON_APPROVAL_MODE=team` believes specs require a second human. In practice alice submits a spec, then issues `curl -XPOST .../pmo/specs/{id}/approve` with no headers; the middleware mints the synthetic identity `local-user`, `"local-user" != "alice"` so the 403 never fires, and the spec transitions to `approved` and becomes fireable into plan generation. The segregation-of-duties control that gates every spec entering the engine is defeated by omitting a header. docs/api-reference.md:1995 compounds this by telling operators "In `BATON_APPROVAL_MODE=team` mode the header is required for approve/bounce operations" — neither handler requires it, and `bounce_spec_draft` (spec_queue.py:275-289) performs no approval-mode check at all.
proposed_fix: In `_resolve_user_id`, honour the documented contract: when `self.approval_mode == "team"` and neither `X-Baton-User` nor a Bearer token resolves an identity, return `""` and have the middleware leave `request.state.user_id` unset/empty. Then in `approve_spec_draft` (and `bounce_spec_draft`, per the docs) reject an empty actor in team mode with 401 before the inequality check. Separately, move `_APPROVAL_MODE` off module scope into `UserIdentityMiddleware.__init__` (`os.environ.get(...)` at construction time) so `create_app()` picks up the current environment rather than whatever was set when the module first imported.
test_strategy: Replace the tautological assertion at tests/api/test_specs_api.py:233 with three hard assertions against an app built with `UserIdentityMiddleware(approval_mode="team")`: (1) submitter alice self-approving with `X-Baton-User: alice` → exactly 403; (2) an approve request with **no** identity headers → 401 (today: 200, and the draft's status is `approved`); (3) `X-Baton-User: bob` → 200. Add a fourth asserting `create_app()` after `monkeypatch.setenv("BATON_APPROVAL_MODE","team")` actually yields team behaviour, proving the import-time freeze is gone.

title: GitHub importer interpolates an unvalidated ref into the API URL, redirecting the server's GITHUB_TOKEN at arbitrary GitHub endpoints
evidence:
`GitHubIssuesImporter._parse_ref` returns the caller's string unchanged when it is neither a bare number nor a URL containing an `issues/` segment (importers.py:119-130):

    parts = ref.rstrip("/").split("/")
    for i, part in enumerate(parts):
        if part == "issues" and i + 1 < len(parts):
            return parts[i + 1]
    return ref                       # line 130 — arbitrary string passthrough

That value is interpolated straight into the request path (importers.py:101-102) and sent with the server's token (lines 106-110):

    url = f"https://api.github.com/repos/{self._owner}/{self._repo}/issues/{issue_number}"
    if self._token:
        headers["Authorization"] = f"Bearer {self._token}"

Verified that httpx applies RFC 3986 dot-segment removal, so traversal collapses server-side before the request goes out:

    >>> httpx.Request('GET','https://api.github.com/repos/o/r/issues/' + '../../../../user/repos').url
    URL('https://api.github.com/user/repos')
    >>> GitHubIssuesImporter('o','r')._parse_ref('../../../../user')
    '../../../../user'

`ImportSpecDraftRequest` (agent_baton/api/models/requests.py:721-725) constrains `ref` only with `min_length=1`; `owner`/`repo` default to `""` with no validation either. The route at spec_queue.py:404 calls `importer.fetch(req.ref)` with the raw value.
why_it_matters: `POST /api/v1/pmo/specs/import` is reachable by any PMO caller, but `GITHUB_TOKEN` is a *server-side* credential whose scope is typically much broader than the caller's. A caller sends `{"source":"github","owner":"o","repo":"r","ref":"../../../../repos/private-org/secret/issues/1"}`; httpx normalises this to `https://api.github.com/repos/private-org/secret/issues/1`, the server's token authorises it, and `fetch()` copies `data["title"]` and `data["body"]` into a new spec draft that is returned verbatim in the 201 response body. That is authenticated read of any GitHub resource the daemon's token can reach, exfiltrated through the API response — a confused-deputy against a repo the caller was never entitled to. Even without a token it is unbounded SSRF against `api.github.com` paths. Secondary correctness effect: garbage refs such as `"  "` silently normalise to `''`, producing `.../issues/` → a 404 surfaced as a generic 502 "Upstream source returned an error" with no hint that the ref was malformed.
proposed_fix: Make `_parse_ref` total and fail closed: accept only `^\d+$` after extracting the trailing segment, and raise `ValueError(f"Invalid GitHub issue ref: {ref!r}; expected an issue number or an issue URL")` otherwise. Validate `owner`/`repo` against `^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$` in `GitHubIssuesImporter.__init__` (and require them non-empty for `source="github"` in `ImportSpecDraftRequest`, which today lets them default to `""`). Map the resulting `ValueError` to HTTP 400 in `import_spec_draft` so the caller sees a usable message rather than a 502. Apply the same digits-only check to `AzureDevOpsImporter.fetch`'s `ref.strip().lstrip("#")` (importers.py:186), which has the identical passthrough.
test_strategy: A unit test asserting `GitHubIssuesImporter('o','r')._parse_ref` raises `ValueError` for `'../../../../user'`, `'not-a-number'`, `'  '`, and `'5/../../x'`, and returns `'5'` / `'9'` for `'5'` and `'https://github.com/x/y/issues/9'`. An API test posting `{"source":"github","owner":"o","repo":"r","ref":"../../../../user"}` must assert 400 and that `httpx.get` was never called (patch it and assert `not called`) — today the call fires against `https://api.github.com/user`. A third test asserting `POST /pmo/specs/import` with `source='github'` and empty `owner` returns 422.

title: Eleven manager-mode config keys are scaffolded and validated but never read by any engine code
evidence:
`_MANAGER_TEMPLATE` in config_cmd.py:81-160 is the profile `baton config` writes for users, and `ManagerConfig` validates every key in it. But grepping each key across `agent_baton/` (excluding the config module itself) shows eleven keys whose *only* occurrence is that scaffold string — no engine module ever reads them:

    require_role_cards            -> only cli/commands/config_cmd.py:96
    require_workstream_owners     -> only cli/commands/config_cmd.py:97
    allow_talent_builder          -> only cli/commands/config_cmd.py:99
    assumptions_policy            -> only cli/commands/config_cmd.py:88
    manager_decision_threshold    -> only cli/commands/config_cmd.py:87
    missing_pack_policy           -> only cli/commands/config_cmd.py:134
    missing_gate_policy           -> only cli/commands/config_cmd.py:153
    allow_smoke_fallback          -> only cli/commands/config_cmd.py:152
    dedupe_knowledge_across_session -> only cli/commands/config_cmd.py:118
    include_full_prior_outputs    -> only cli/commands/config_cmd.py:116
    summarize_prior_outputs       -> only cli/commands/config_cmd.py:117

For contrast, the keys that *are* wired resolve to real call sites — e.g. `require_allowed_paths`/`require_scope_contracts` at charter.py:182 and :187, `scope_expansion_policy` at scope.py:60 (12 hits), `allow_cross_scope_edits`/`out_of_scope_policy` at charter.py:162-168. The loader's contract makes the silence worse: `_Section` uses `ConfigDict(extra="ignore")` (manager.py:44) and `_validated` only warns on *unknown top-level* keys (manager.py:160-168), so a known-but-inert key is accepted with no warning at all.
why_it_matters: An operator who sets `gates.missing_gate_policy: fail` and `gates.allow_smoke_fallback: false` in `.claude/baton.yaml` — believing they have hardened gating so a missing gate blocks the plan — gets exactly the default behaviour, with the config loading cleanly and `config.warnings` empty. Same for `team.require_role_cards: false` (role cards are built regardless), `context.include_full_prior_outputs: true` (bundles still summarise), and `knowledge_packs.missing_pack_policy: ignore` (still proposes). This is configuration that reads as a governance control and is in fact decoration — the strongest form of the repo's own 'failing silently' anti-pattern, since the failure mode is that a safety setting appears to have been accepted.
proposed_fix: Either wire or withdraw each key. For the gate keys, `PhasePolicyApplier`/the gate-derivation path should consult `config.gates.missing_gate_policy` and `allow_smoke_fallback` before falling back to smoke. For the context keys, `ContextBundleBuilder` should branch on `include_full_prior_outputs`/`summarize_prior_outputs`/`dedupe_knowledge_across_session` when assembling prior-phase handoff. For keys with no near-term implementation, remove them from `_MANAGER_TEMPLATE` and add an explicit `_UNIMPLEMENTED_KEYS` set in `ManagerConfig._validated` that appends to `config.warnings` (e.g. "team.require_role_cards is accepted but not yet enforced") so `baton config validate` tells the truth.
test_strategy: A meta-test in `tests/manager/test_manager_config.py` that walks every leaf field of `ManagerConfig` and asserts each field name appears in at least one `agent_baton/**/*.py` file outside `core/config/manager.py` and `cli/commands/config_cmd.py` — failing today with the eleven names above. Plus a behavioural test per key that is claimed to be wired: e.g. build a plan with `gates.missing_gate_policy="fail"` and a phase with no gate, and assert the planner raises/blocks rather than warning.

title: tests/federate/ covers only the rubric — importers, SpecDraftStore, and the enrich cost path have zero unit tests

Grepping the whole suite for the package finds three files: `tests/federate/test_rubric.py`, `tests/api/test_specs_api.py`, and `tests/test_federated_sync_integration.py` (an unrelated sync subsystem). Nothing anywhere imports `agent_baton.core.federate.importers` or exercises `SpecDraftStore`'s transition guards directly.

The single test that touches `enrich()` is test_rubric.py:93-119 (`test_enrich_includes_spec_quality`), and it asserts only step 4's output:

    assert data.spec_quality is not None
    assert "score" in data.spec_quality
    ...
    assert 0 <= data.spec_quality["score"] <= 100

It never inspects `est_usd_*`, `breakdown`, or `cost_confidence`, which is precisely why the `NameError` at enrich.py:137 has been shipping undetected. `tests/api/test_specs_api.py:60` deliberately neuters the code under test in every route test — `monkeypatch.setattr(_enrich_mod, "_run_enrichment", lambda spec_id, store: None)` — so the API suite cannot catch it either. test_strategy: Coverage assertion: running `pytest tests/federate --cov=agent_baton.core.federate` must report >80% line coverage for `importers.py` and `spec_draft_store.py` (both near 0% today). title: Documented spec-queue auth contract and cost_confidence value do not match the implementation
evidence:
docs/api-reference.md:1994-1996 states: "In `BATON_APPROVAL_MODE=team` mode the header is required for approve/bounce operations, and a user may not approve their own spec (returns 403)." Neither handler requires the header: `approve_spec_draft` only compares identities (spec_queue.py:235-243), and `bounce_spec_draft` (spec_queue.py:265-289) contains no reference to `approval_mode` at all — its only checks are 404 and the `status != "enriched"` 409.

docs/api-reference.md:2132 documents `| cost_confidence | string | `default` or `calibrated` |`, but enrich.py:157 sets `cost_confidence = "high"`, and the model docstring (agent_baton/models/spec_draft.py:49) agrees with the code: "Either ``\"high\"`` (history-calibrated) or ``\"default\"``". `pmo-ui/src/components/SpecQueuePanel.tsx:814` renders the raw string, so the UI would display the undocumented value.

test_strategy: A test asserting `POST /pmo/specs/{id}/bounce` with no identity header under `approval_mode="team"` returns 401, matching the documented contract (today: 200).
