title: Budget-tier auto-apply guardrail is bypassed by the planner's direct read of budget-recommendations.json
evidence: `BudgetTuner.auto_apply_recommendations()` (budget_tuner.py:290) documents the guardrail and claims its caller: "Guardrail: only DOWNGRADE recommendations are returned. Budget upgrades (to more expensive tiers) are never auto-applied because increasing spend without human oversight violates the cost-safety principle. This method is called by ImprovementLoop during the closed-loop cycle...". Grep shows `ImprovementLoop` never calls it — the only caller is `agent_baton/cli/commands/improve/budget.py:46`. What `run_cycle` actually does is loop.py:205-206: `tuner.save_recommendations()`, and `save_recommendations()` (budget_tuner.py:272-288) writes `self.analyze()` verbatim — upgrades included, no confidence filter. The planner then reads that file with no filter at all: `select_budget_tier()` in risk_and_policy.py:248-255 is `recs = budget_tuner.load_recommendations(); if recs: for rec in recs: if rec.task_type == task_type: return rec.recommended_tier` wrapped in `except Exception: pass`. `IntelligentPlanner._select_budget_tier` (planner.py:796) calls exactly that. Meanwhile the loop's own classifier `_should_auto_apply()` (loop.py:286-322, enforcing `risk == "low"` and `confidence >= auto_apply_threshold`) feeds `_apply_recommendation()` (loop.py:328-331), which only does `rec.status = "applied"; self._proposals.update_status(...)` — a status string nothing else reads. `merge_cross_project_cost_signals()` (budget_tuner.py:324+) writes `source="central"` rows into the same file, so cross-project signals also land on the unfiltered path.
why_it_matters: A single low-confidence UPGRADE recommendation (e.g. 3 usage records, confidence 0.3, `lean` -> `full`) written by any `baton improve`/`run_cycle` invocation is picked up by the very next `baton plan` for that task_type and silently raises the budget tier — permanently increasing spend with no human sign-off, no `escalated` entry acted on, and no log line. The improvement report will list the rec under `escalated`, telling the operator it was NOT applied, while the planner has already applied it. Conversely the `_should_auto_apply` guardrails and `auto_apply_threshold` config have zero effect on budget tiers, so the documented safety mechanism is decorative.
proposed_fix: Make the read path enforce the guardrail rather than the write path: (1) have `select_budget_tier()` filter to recommendations that are downgrades or that carry an explicit `applied=True`/`status="applied"` marker AND meet a confidence threshold, instead of returning the first task_type match; (2) replace the blanket `except Exception: pass` with a logged, typed except; (3) in `ImprovementLoop.run_cycle`, stop calling `tuner.save_recommendations()` unconditionally — call `tuner.auto_apply_recommendations(threshold=self._config.auto_apply_threshold)` and persist only that filtered set as the planner-visible file, writing the full analysis to a separate advisory file for `baton improve budget` to display.
test_strategy: Write a usage log that yields one UPGRADE recommendation (`current_tier="lean"`, `recommended_tier="full"`, `confidence=0.3`) for task_type X. Run `ImprovementLoop.run_cycle(force=True)`, assert the report lists that rec under `escalated` and not `auto_applied`, then call `IntelligentPlanner._select_budget_tier("X", agent_count=1)` and assert it returns `"lean"` (the agent-count default), NOT `"full"`. Add the mirror case: a DOWNGRADE with confidence 0.9 must be honoured by `select_budget_tier`.

title: Immune sweeper and triage call ClaudeCodeLauncher.launch() with the wrong signature and never await it — every real sweep silently returns no finding
evidence: `Sweeper.sweep()` invokes the launcher as `result = self._launcher.launch(agent_name=agent_name, prompt=prompt, cwd_override=...)` (sweeper.py:133-139), immediately followed by `except Exception as exc: _log.warning("Sweeper: launch failed for %s/%s: %s", ...); return None` (sweeper.py:140-146). The production launcher wired in by `_build_launcher()` (daemon_immune_cmd.py:417-424) is `ClaudeCodeLauncher`, whose real signature I probed with `inspect`: `async: True` / `(self, agent_name: str, model: str, prompt: str, step_id: str = '', mcp_servers=None, cwd_override=None, task_id: str = '')` — `model` is required and has no default (claude_launcher.py:484-493). So the call raises `TypeError: launch() missing 1 required positional argument: 'model'`, which the blanket `except Exception` swallows into `return None` (= "target is clean"). Even with `model` supplied, `launch` is a coroutine function called without `await`, so `_parse_result` would receive a coroutine object: not `str`, no `.output`, not `dict` -> `text = str(raw)` -> `json.loads` fails -> `return None`. `FindingTriage._dispatch_autofix_micro_agent` has the identical defective call at triage.py:169-175. Tests never catch this because the launcher is a bare `MagicMock()` accepting any kwargs (`tests/test_immune_daemon.py:87-88`: `launcher = MagicMock(); launcher.launch.return_value = None`). The fallback `_StubLauncher` (daemon_immune_cmd.py:428-431) also just logs a warning and returns `None`.
why_it_matters: An operator runs `baton daemon-immune start`. The CLI prints "Immune daemon running (PID …) cap=$5.00/day", `baton daemon-immune status` shows `Status: running` with a fresh `Last tick`, and `Findings: 0`. Every sweep in fact aborts on a TypeError logged at WARNING (invisible under default logging), every target is marked `found_issue=False`, and `daemon.record_immune_spend()` still books the full 12K-in/1K-out estimate per tick (daemon.py:218) — so the daily budget is consumed by sweeps that never executed, and after the cap trips the daemon sleeps until 00:00 UTC. Zero findings is indistinguishable from a clean codebase.
proposed_fix: Give `Sweeper`/`FindingTriage` a narrow launcher adapter that (a) passes the required `model` (Haiku/Sonnet per `_KIND_AGENT` tier) and (b) drives the coroutine to completion via `asyncio.run(...)` / an owned loop, returning the `LaunchResult`. Narrow `except Exception` to the transport errors the launcher actually raises and let `TypeError`/`AttributeError` propagate (or re-raise after logging at ERROR) so a wiring mismatch is loud. Only call `budget.record_immune_spend()` when a launch actually completed, and surface consecutive launch failures as a bead so the operator sees them.
test_strategy: Assert the contract, not a mock: instantiate the real `ClaudeCodeLauncher` (or use `inspect.signature`) and assert `Sweeper.sweep()` completes against it without raising and without a swallowed `TypeError` — e.g. patch only the subprocess boundary, return a canned JSON payload, and assert `sweep()` returns a `SweepFinding`. Add a regression test asserting `inspect.signature(ClaudeCodeLauncher.launch).bind(...)` succeeds with exactly the kwargs the sweeper passes, so a future signature change fails the suite. Separately assert `budget.record_immune_spend` is NOT called when the launch raises.

title: Immune daemon's sweep queue is never seeded in production, so next_target() always returns None
evidence: `SweepScheduler.seed(paths, kind)` (scheduler.py:115) is the only writer of new `immune_queue` rows. A repo-wide grep for `.seed(` outside the scheduler returns only test files (`tests/test_immune_daemon.py:85`, `tests/test_immune_scheduler.py:185`, `tests/test_run_token_ceiling.py:316`). `_handle_start` in daemon_immune_cmd.py:182 constructs `SweepScheduler(project_root=project_dir, conn=conn)` and never calls `seed()`; no other production module references `immune_queue` (only `core/storage/schema.py:1091` creates the table). The daemon loop therefore hits `target = self.scheduler.next_target()` (daemon.py:190) -> `None` -> `_log.debug("ImmuneDaemon: no targets ready — sleeping")` -> `continue`, forever.
why_it_matters: `baton daemon-immune start` on any real project starts a daemon whose queue table is empty, so it does nothing at all — no sweep, no bead, no finding — while printing "Immune daemon running" and writing a `daemon_state.json` with `status: running` every 30 s. There is no command to populate the queue and no documentation telling a user how, so the entire immune subsystem is unreachable from the CLI. This also masks finding #2: even with the launcher fixed, nothing would sweep.
proposed_fix: Seed on start: in `_handle_start`, after building the scheduler, walk the project for candidate files (respecting .gitignore, capped) and call `scheduler.seed(paths, kind)` for each kind in `config.sweep_kinds`; re-seed newly-added files each tick or on a slower cadence. Expose it explicitly as `baton daemon-immune seed [--kind K] [--path P]` so operators can scope it, and log the resulting `scheduler.queue_size()` at start. If the queue is empty at start-up, print a loud warning rather than silently idling.
test_strategy: Integration test: create a temp project with a couple of .py files and a fresh baton.db, invoke the `daemon-immune start` handler with a stub sweeper and `--tick-sec 0`, shut down after one tick, and assert (a) `SweepScheduler(...).queue_size() > 0` and (b) the sweeper received at least one `SweepTarget`. Assert the start path emits a warning when no targets could be enqueued.

title: SweepScheduler.next_target() ignores the defer window, so the 30-day/7-day re-sweep policy never takes effect
evidence: `mark_swept()` writes a FUTURE timestamp as `last_swept_at`: `defer_days = _DEFER_ISSUE_DAYS if found_issue else _DEFER_NO_ISSUE_DAYS` (7/30, scheduler.py:27-28) then `SET last_swept_at = ?` with `_future_str(defer_days)` (scheduler.py:186-193). But `next_target()` has no time predicate at all: `SELECT path, kind, last_swept_at, priority FROM immune_queue ORDER BY last_swept_at ASC, priority DESC LIMIT 1` (scheduler.py:145-152). Its own docstring claims "Return the next sweep target or ``None`` if none are ready" and the daemon's `if target is None: _log.debug("ImmuneDaemon: no targets ready — sleeping")` (daemon.py:191-194) is written against that contract — but `None` is returned only when the table is empty, so the "not ready" branch is dead code.
why_it_matters: Once the queue is populated, the daemon round-robins the entire corpus every `tick_interval_sec` (300 s default) forever instead of honouring the 30-day defer: a 200-file queue is fully re-swept every ~17 hours rather than monthly. Each sweep books `record_immune_spend()` (daemon.py:218), so the $5/day cap is exhausted daily by redundant re-scans of files that were already found clean, and `_sleep_until_budget_reset()` then parks the daemon until midnight — meaning genuinely stale targets are never reached because the budget is spent on the head of the queue.
proposed_fix: Add the readiness predicate to `next_target()`: `WHERE last_swept_at <= :now` (with `:now` = `_utcnow_str()`, safe because both are ISO-8601 Z strings that sort lexicographically), keeping the existing ORDER BY. Optionally rename the column to `next_sweep_at` so the semantics ('when it becomes eligible again') match the value being stored.
test_strategy: Seed one target, call `mark_swept(target, found_issue=False)`, then assert `next_target()` returns `None` (deferred 30 days). Then rewrite the row's `last_swept_at` to a past timestamp and assert `next_target()` returns the target again. Add a daemon-level test asserting that after every seeded target has been swept once, the next tick performs zero `sweeper.sweep()` calls and zero `record_immune_spend()` calls.

title: Executor._persist_event's JSONL write is unguarded despite a docstring promising best-effort, so a disk error aborts execution and starves later bus subscribers
evidence: `_persist_event` is subscribed to `"*"` on the shared bus (executor.py:540-541 and 555-556). Its docstring states: "Both writes are best-effort; a failure in either path logs a warning and does not crash execution." (executor.py:5675-5677). The body only guards the SQLite path — `self._event_persistence.append(event)` at executor.py:5683 has no try/except, while `self._storage.append_event(event)` is wrapped at 5686-5692. `EventPersistence.append` does `self._dir.mkdir(...)` and `path.open("a")` + `f.write(line)` (events/persistence.py:71-76) with no error handling, so ENOSPC / EACCES / read-only FS raises `OSError`. `EventBus.publish` propagates by design — "Handlers execute inline -- if a handler raises, the exception propagates to the publisher" (bus.py:78-80) — and iterates subscribers in registration order (bus.py:93-95), so the raise also prevents `_on_event_for_telemetry` and any SSE/webhook subscriber registered later from ever seeing that event.
why_it_matters: On a full or read-only disk (or a `.claude/team-context` mounted noexec/ro in CI), the very first `bus.publish(...)` from `Worker`/`ExecutionEngine` raises `OSError` out of `publish()` into the middle of the dispatch path, crashing the run with a stack trace that points at the event log rather than the real problem — the exact opposite of the documented behaviour, and unrecoverable by `baton execute resume` because state may be half-written. The subscriber-starvation effect is worse in the API server: one raising handler stops webhook delivery and SSE fan-out for that event with no log line anywhere.
proposed_fix: Wrap the JSONL append in the same try/except-and-log pattern already used for the storage write (executor.py:5686-5692). Independently, harden the bus: catch exceptions per-handler in `EventBus.publish`, log them with the subscription id and topic, and continue to the remaining subscribers, so no single subscriber can starve the others or crash the publisher — then update the `publish` docstring to match.
test_strategy: Construct an `ExecutionEngine` with a bus, monkeypatch `EventPersistence.append` to raise `OSError("No space left on device")`, publish an event, and assert (a) `publish()` does not raise, (b) a warning was logged, and (c) a second subscriber registered after `_persist_event` still received the event. Add a bus-level unit test: subscribe a raising handler then a recording handler, publish, assert the recording handler still fired.

title: EventBus.replay() is memory-only and never rehydrated, so 'rebuild state after a crash' is impossible and history grows unbounded
evidence: `replay()` documents itself as "Used by the execution engine to rebuild state after a crash or to catch up a late-joining subscriber" (bus.py:145-146) but iterates only `self._history` (bus.py:161), an in-process list appended to in `publish()` (bus.py:91) and initialised empty in `__init__` (bus.py:67). Nothing ever loads it from disk: grep for `_history`/`rehydrate` across `agent_baton/api/` and `agent_baton/core/events/` returns only the bus itself, and `init_dependencies` simply does `_bus = bus if bus is not None else EventBus()` (deps.py:117). The only production caller is the SSE route: `existing = bus.replay(task_id=task_id)` (api/routes/events.py:98). `clear()` is annotated "Primarily for testing" (bus.py:183) and there is no cap on `_history`.
why_it_matters: Two concrete failures. (1) A client opening `GET /api/v1/events/{task_id}/stream` for a task executed by the CLI — a different process — receives an empty replay and only sees events published after it connected, even though the same events are durably on disk in `.claude/team-context/executions/<task>/events/*.jsonl` and in the SQLite `events` table; the same happens for any task that ran before the last `baton serve` restart. Clients silently render an incomplete timeline with no error. (2) In a long-lived `baton serve`, `_history` retains every event ever published for the process lifetime, so memory grows without bound.
proposed_fix: Back `replay()` with the durable stores instead of memory: give `EventBus` an optional `EventPersistence`/storage reader and have `replay(task_id, from_seq, topic_pattern)` merge on-disk events with any in-memory tail, de-duplicating on `event_id`. Independently, bound `_history` with a `collections.deque(maxlen=N)` (configurable) so the in-memory tail cannot grow without limit, and update the docstrings so the durability story is stated accurately.
test_strategy: Write events for task T through `EventPersistence` (simulating a prior process), construct a fresh `EventBus` wired to that events dir, and assert `bus.replay(task_id="T")` returns those events in sequence order — currently it returns `[]`. Add an API test that hits the SSE stream for a task whose events exist only on disk and asserts the replay frames are emitted. Add a memory test: publish `maxlen + 100` events and assert `len(bus.history()) <= maxlen` while `replay()` still returns the full set from disk.

title: README documents an experimental 'Predictive watcher' feature flag in core/intel/ that was deleted, and the wrong immune CLI command name
evidence: README lists twice: `| Predictive watcher | feature flag in `core/intel/` | Wave 6.2 Part C stub |` (lines 713 and 1026), under a heading stating "These surfaces emit stub warnings to stderr on invocation". Migration v43 says the opposite: "the Wave 6.2 Part C predictive computation subsystem have been deleted" (schema.py:1318-1320), and `ls agent_baton/core/intel/` contains only bead_synthesizer, context_harvester, debate, handoff_synthesizer, knowledge_ranker, phase_summary — a case-insensitive grep for `predictive|watcher` across `agent_baton/` returns exactly one hit, that schema comment. Separately README:755 documents `baton daemon immune start/stop/status`, but the parser registers the command as `daemon-immune` (daemon_immune_cmd.py:47) and `baton daemon --help` lists only `{start,status,stop,list}` — I ran it. The same section claims the experimental surfaces "emit stub warnings to stderr"; `baton daemon-immune start` emits no such warning, it prints "Immune daemon running (PID …)".
why_it_matters: A user following the README looks in `core/intel/` for a predictive-watcher flag that does not exist and cannot exist, and types `baton daemon immune start` which fails with an argparse error. Worse, the README's blanket "emits stub warnings on invocation" claim means an operator who starts the immune daemon and sees no warning reasonably concludes it is functioning — which, per findings #2 and #3, it is not. Root CLAUDE.md makes README/CLI-reference updates mandatory after significant work.
proposed_fix: Delete both Predictive-watcher rows from the README experimental tables (the subsystem is gone as of schema v43). Correct `baton daemon immune …` to `baton daemon-immune …` at README:755 and anywhere else, or add an `immune` subcommand alias under the existing `daemon` parser and keep the documented spelling. Replace the blanket "emit stub warnings to stderr" sentence with per-feature accuracy, and make `daemon-immune start` actually print an EXPERIMENTAL warning to stderr so the README's claim becomes true.
test_strategy: Add a docs-contract test that (a) asserts every command string appearing in a README CLI table resolves against the built argparse parser (catching `daemon immune`), and (b) asserts each feature named in the Experimental tables maps to an importable module or a defined env flag (catching Predictive watcher). Add a CLI test asserting `daemon-immune start` writes an 'EXPERIMENTAL' line to stderr.

title: PreToolUse secret guard in templates/settings.json never blocks .env writes
evidence:
templates/settings.json ships this PreToolUse hook (matcher `Write|Edit`):

    bash -c 'FILE="$CLAUDE_TOOL_INPUT_FILE_PATH"; if echo "$FILE" | grep -qE "(/(\\.|^)\.env($|/)|/secrets/|/node_modules/|\\.(pem|key)$|/\.credentials)"; then echo "BLOCKED: Write to protected path: $FILE" >&2; exit 2; fi; exit 0'

I executed the exact command string parsed out of the JSON. Results:
  FILE='/home/u/proj/.env'  -> rc=0 (ALLOWED)
  FILE='.env'               -> rc=0 (ALLOWED)
  FILE='/tmp/.env'          -> rc=0 (ALLOWED)
  FILE='secrets/x.txt'      -> rc=0 (ALLOWED)
  FILE='/x/secrets/y'       -> rc=2 (blocked)
  var UNSET                 -> rc=0 (ALLOWED)

Two independent causes. (1) After bash double-quote processing `\\.` collapses to `\.`, so the branch is `/(\.|^)\.env` — a literal slash, then a dot-or-`^`, then a dot, then `env`. It requires TWO dots: `echo /proj/..env | grep -qE '(/(\.|^)\.env($|/))'` matches, `echo /proj/.env | ...` returns 0 matches. The `^` alternative is unreachable because it sits after a required `/`. (2) `CLAUDE_TOOL_INPUT_FILE_PATH` is not a variable the hook runtime sets — the repo's own hook implementation reads the path from the stdin JSON instead (`agent_baton/cli/commands/govern/policy_check.py:48`: `fp = tool_input.get("file_path") or tool_input.get("path", "")`), confirming stdin is the real interface. With the variable unset, `FILE` is empty and the hook always exits 0.

The same broken `FILE="$CLAUDE_TOOL_INPUT_FILE_PATH"` idiom is generated for per-step path enforcement at `agent_baton/core/engine/dispatcher.py:1079`, so `PlanStep.allowed_paths`/`blocked_paths` are also unenforced.

references/hooks-enforcement.md:15 advertises "Agent writes to .env or secrets/ | PreToolUse hooks block the write", and :191-193 tells the user to validate by asking Claude to "Create a .env file with DATABASE_URL=test" and asserts "The PreToolUse hooks should block it". That documented smoke test fails, and :193 misattributes the failure to the hook not being loaded.
why_it_matters: A user installs the templates, runs the documented `.env` smoke test, sees the write go through, and follows the doc's advice to check JSON validity and session restart — all of which pass. They conclude the hook is fine or give up, while every agent in the project can freely write to `.env`, `.credentials`, and relative `secrets/` paths. The only remaining defence is `baton policy-check`, which requires `baton classify --activate` to have been run; on a fresh install with no active policy the fast inline guard is the advertised first line of defence and it is a no-op.
proposed_fix: Stop depending on a nonexistent env var: read the PreToolUse JSON from stdin, e.g. `FILE=$(python3 -c 'import sys,json; print(json.load(sys.stdin).get("tool_input",{}).get("file_path",""))')`, or delete the inline hook entirely and rely solely on `baton policy-check`, which already parses stdin correctly. Fix the regex to `(^|/)\.env($|/|\.)|(^|/)secrets/|(^|/)node_modules/|\.(pem|key)$|(^|/)\.credentials` so relative paths and single-dot `.env` match. Apply the same stdin fix to `PromptDispatcher.build_path_enforcement` (dispatcher.py:1079). Correct hooks-enforcement.md:193 to list "regex does not match your path" as a cause.
test_strategy: A test that shells out to the actual command string extracted from `templates/settings.json` (not a hand-written copy) and asserts returncode == 2 for each of `.env`, `/abs/path/.env`, `secrets/creds.txt`, `/p/.credentials`, `key.pem`, and returncode == 0 for `src/app.py` — feeding the path through the same channel the real hook runtime uses (stdin JSON). A separate test must assert the guard denies (non-zero) rather than allows when the path cannot be resolved, so an interface change fails closed. Add a parallel test for `build_path_enforcement` asserting a blocked path in `step.blocked_paths` yields exit 2.

title: agents/CLAUDE.md and references/CLAUDE.md are packaged and installed as agent/reference definitions, creating a phantom "CLAUDE" agent
evidence:
`agent_baton/_bundled_agents/` contains `CLAUDE.md` (a byte-for-byte mirror of `agents/CLAUDE.md`, which starts `# agents/ — distributable agent definitions`, no frontmatter). `AgentRegistry._load_bundled_agents` filters only on `if not name.endswith(".md")` (registry.py:141) and `load_directory` globs `directory.glob("*.md")` (registry.py:87) with no exclusion list. Probe:

    >>> r = AgentRegistry(); r._load_bundled_agents()
    31
    >>> r.get('CLAUDE')
    AgentDefinition(name='CLAUDE', description='', model='', tools=[], category=AgentCategory.ENGINEERING)

`baton agents` renders it to the user:

    Engineering:
      CLAUDE                              []

`baton install --scope project --source <repo> --verify` in a clean temp dir prints:

    Installed: 31 agents + 21 references + 3 agent templates to project
    Verification found 1 issue(s):
      - Agent CLAUDE.md: missing YAML frontmatter

(31/21, not the documented 30/20 — `agents/CLAUDE.md:3` says "30 agent definitions", `references/CLAUDE.md:3` says "20 reference procedures".) The installer copied the very file its own `--verify` then flags, and the process still exits 0. `.claude/agents/CLAUDE.md` is landed in the user's project and re-registers as an agent on project load.

The project already knows the rule — `AgentValidator.validate_directory` explicitly skips it (validator.py:261-264):

    _NON_AGENT_FILES = {"CLAUDE.md", "README.md"}
    for md_file in sorted(directory.glob("*.md")):
        if md_file.name in _NON_AGENT_FILES:
            continue

The registry, the bundled-resource loader, and the installer apply no such filter.
why_it_matters: Every user gets a bogus `CLAUDE` agent in category ENGINEERING with `model=''`, `tools=[]`, and a maintainer-only build doc (referencing `scripts/sync_bundled_agents.sh`, which does not exist in their project) as its system prompt. It appears in `baton agents`, in `registry.names`, and in `by_category(AgentCategory.ENGINEERING)` — so anything that iterates engineering agents can select it, and a dispatch would ship an empty model and the wrong prompt. A user running the documented `--verify` health check on a brand-new install is told their install is broken, by a defect the installer created.
proposed_fix: Hoist `_NON_AGENT_FILES` out of `validator.validate_directory` into a shared constant and apply it in all three places: `AgentRegistry.load_directory` (registry.py:87), the bundled-resource iteration (registry.py:141), and the copy loops in `install._cmd_install` (install.py:258 for agents, install.py:265 for references). Also exclude `CLAUDE.md` from `scripts/sync_bundled_agents.sh` so it stops shipping in the wheel, and make `_verify_install` exit non-zero when it finds issues.
test_strategy: Assert `'CLAUDE' not in AgentRegistry().load_default_paths()`-populated `registry.names` and that a registry loaded from a directory containing `CLAUDE.md` + `README.md` + one real agent reports exactly 1 agent. Assert `baton install --scope project` into a tmp dir produces no `.claude/agents/CLAUDE.md` and no `.claude/references/CLAUDE.md`, that the printed agent count equals the number of frontmatter-bearing files, and that `--verify` on that fresh install reports zero issues and exits 0.

title: baton install never installs templates/skills, packs, specs, or playbooks — the installed CLAUDE.md points at things that are not there
evidence:
`_cmd_install` builds `skills_dir = base / "skills"` (install.py:240) and includes it in the `mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)` loop (install.py:248), but the file-copy section only ever copies `agents_src`, `refs_src`, `agent_templates_src` (`templates/agents/`), `templates/CLAUDE.md`, and `templates/settings.json`. There is no copy loop for `templates/skills/`, `templates/packs/`, `templates/specs/`, or `templates/playbooks/`. A repo-wide grep for `templates/skills` in `agent_baton/**/*.py` returns no hits at all — nothing else installs them either.

Real install into a clean temp dir:

    $ baton install --scope project --source /home/user/agent-baton
    $ find .claude -maxdepth 2 -type d
    .claude/agents .claude/knowledge .claude/references .claude/skills .claude/team-context .claude/templates/agents
    $ ls -A .claude/skills
    (empty)
    $ ls -A .claude/packs
    ls: cannot access '.claude/packs': No such file or directory

The file that gets copied verbatim to the user's project root as `CLAUDE.md` then says:
- templates/CLAUDE.md:12 — "Use `/baton-help` for the full CLI reference."
- templates/CLAUDE.md:264 — "Org-level assurance packs are stored in `.claude/packs/`."

`/baton-help` is `templates/skills/baton-help/SKILL.md`, which is never copied; the same holds for `baton-beads` and `baton-learn`. `.claude/packs/` is never created and `templates/packs/{phi-hipaa,secure-coding-owasp}` never ship, so the `baton packs validate` / `baton packs list` commands the same file recommends at :268-270 run against an empty registry.
why_it_matters: On a fresh `baton install`, a user or agent following the installed CLAUDE.md types `/baton-help` and gets nothing — the single documented entry point to the CLI reference is dead. The empty `.claude/skills/` directory makes the failure look like a corrupted install rather than a missing feature. Three skills and two reference assurance packs that exist in the repo are unreachable to every installed user, and `baton packs list` shows nothing despite the docs implying seeded packs.
proposed_fix: Add copy loops in `_cmd_install` for `templates/skills/` (recursive, preserving the `<skill>/SKILL.md` layout) into `base/"skills"`, and for `templates/packs/` into `base/"packs"`; include `specs/` and `playbooks/` or drop the directories from the repo if they are not distributable. Extend `_verify_install` to assert at least one `SKILL.md` under `base/"skills"`. If skills are deliberately not installed, remove the `/baton-help` instruction from templates/CLAUDE.md:12 and stop creating the empty `skills_dir`.
test_strategy: Install into a tmp dir and assert `.claude/skills/baton-help/SKILL.md`, `.claude/skills/baton-beads/SKILL.md`, and `.claude/skills/baton-learn/SKILL.md` all exist and parse as frontmatter. Add a link-integrity test that scans `templates/CLAUDE.md` for `/<slash-command>` references and `.claude/<dir>/` paths and asserts each resolves to something the installer actually creates — so this class of drift fails CI whenever the template or the installer changes.

title: Distributable orchestration contract documents 6 of 9 ActionTypes; INTERACT and FEEDBACK are emitted but appear in no reference
evidence:
`agent_baton/models/execution.py:63-72` defines 9 ActionTypes; the root CLAUDE.md calls the enum a public API. Three of them are absent from every distributable artifact:

    $ for f in references/*.md; do grep -c 'INTERACT\|FEEDBACK\|CHECKPOINT' $f; done
    -> 0 for all 21 files, including baton-engine.md

`references/baton-engine.md:1776` opens "## Action Types — Every call to `baton execute start`, `baton execute next`, or `baton execute resume` returns exactly one action" and then documents only DISPATCH, GATE, COMPLETE, FAILED, WAIT, APPROVAL. `templates/CLAUDE.md:47-48` states "the engine returns DISPATCH, GATE, APPROVAL, WAIT, or COMPLETE actions" and its pseudocode loop (:137-171) branches on exactly DISPATCH/GATE/APPROVAL/COMPLETE/WAIT/FAILED with no fallback branch.

Both missing types are genuinely emitted:
- `executor.py:7256` — `ExecutionAction(action_type=ActionType.INTERACT, ...)` built by `_interact_action` for any step in `interacting` status.
- `executor.py:7467` — `ExecutionAction(action_type=ActionType.FEEDBACK, ...)` built by `_feedback_action` for any phase with unanswered `feedback_questions`.

Separately, `ActionType.CHECKPOINT` (execution.py:72) has zero emit sites anywhere in `agent_baton/` — it is a dead enum member that the root CLAUDE.md advertises as one of the 9 public values, and it falls through `_print_action`'s bare `else:` branch.

Mitigation is partial only: `_print_action` prints a "Respond with: baton execute interact ..." hint (execute.py:798-799) so a careful orchestrator can recover, but the reference it was told to consult contains nothing.
why_it_matters: An orchestrator running in a user project has exactly two sources of truth — the installed `CLAUDE.md` and `.claude/references/baton-engine.md`. When a plan phase carries feedback questions, `baton execute next` returns `ACTION: FEEDBACK`; neither document has a branch for it, so the loop hits an unhandled action and either stalls or improvises a `baton execute next` retry that returns the same action forever. `references/CLAUDE.md` explicitly frames a reference as "a runbook the agent reads while working", and the runbook is incomplete on a path the engine can reach unprompted.
proposed_fix: Add `### INTERACT` and `### FEEDBACK` sections to the Action Types block in `references/baton-engine.md:1776`, each showing the wire format `_print_action` emits (execute.py:752-799) and the corresponding `baton execute feedback --phase-id N --question-id ID --chosen-index N` / `baton execute interact --step-id S --input "..."` responses. Add matching `elif` branches to the templates/CLAUDE.md loop plus a default branch instructing the orchestrator to stop and report any unrecognised action rather than retry. Either wire up CHECKPOINT or delete the enum member and correct the "9 values" claim in the root CLAUDE.md.
test_strategy: A drift test that imports `ActionType`, and for every member asserts (a) the value string appears in `references/baton-engine.md` and `templates/CLAUDE.md`, and (b) the member has at least one `action_type=ActionType.<X>` construction site under `agent_baton/` — so both an undocumented new action type and a dead one fail CI. Plus an integration test driving a plan with `feedback_questions` through `execute next` and asserting the printed block matches the format documented in baton-engine.md.

title: `tools` frontmatter is declared required but never enforced; orchestrator and task-runner ship with no allowlist, and the documented list form skips validation entirely
evidence:
`references/agent-authoring.md:16-21` lists `tools` and `permissionMode` under "Required frontmatter fields", and `agents/CLAUDE.md:26` says "Tools allowlist: include only what's required." Two of the 30 shipped agents violate this. `agents/task-runner.md` frontmatter is complete at 4 lines:

    ---
    name: task-runner
    description: Executes procedural tasks by following shell commands, HTTP requests, and data-formatting instructions exactly as written...
    model: haiku
    ---

No `tools`, no `permissionMode` — so a haiku agent whose own body says "## What you do NOT do — Make architectural decisions / Write application code or refactor" inherits the full tool surface including Write, Edit, and Task. `agents/orchestrator.md:1-9` likewise has `permissionMode: auto-edit` and no `tools`.

The validator does not catch it — `baton validate agents/` reports "Validated 30 files: 29 valid, 1 warnings, 0 errors", and the only warning on task-runner is about a single-line description and a missing `# ` heading. `AgentValidator.validate_file` checks `model` presence ("'model' field should be present") but has no presence check for `tools` at all.

Worse, the tool-name check is string-only (validator.py:182): `if tools_raw is not None and isinstance(tools_raw, str):`. `agents/CLAUDE.md:13` documents the format as a YAML list — `tools: [Read, Write, ...]` — which is exactly the branch that is never validated. Probe:

    tools: [Read, NotARealTool, rm -rf, KubernetesAdmin]
    $ baton validate a/
    Validated 1 file: 1 valid, 0 warnings, 0 errors
why_it_matters: A user or `talent-builder` authors an agent using the list syntax that `agents/CLAUDE.md` documents, typos a tool name or pastes an over-broad set, and `baton validate` green-lights it; the invalid entry is silently dropped or ignored at dispatch and the agent runs with the wrong capability set. Meanwhile `task-runner` — the lowest-judgment agent in the roster, explicitly instructed not to write code — ships with an unrestricted tool grant, so a prompt-injected or ambiguous instruction can drive it into Write/Edit on any file, contradicting both the roster convention and the authoring contract the project publishes.
proposed_fix: Add `tools: Read, Bash, Glob, Grep` (drop Write/Edit) and `permissionMode: default` to `agents/task-runner.md`; add an explicit `tools` line to `agents/orchestrator.md` covering what it actually needs (Read, Glob, Grep, Bash, Task/Agent, TodoWrite). In `validator.py`, emit a warning when `tools` is absent and normalise the list form before the name check — replace the `isinstance(tools_raw, str)` guard with a branch that also handles `list`, matching the normalisation `AgentRegistry._parse_agent_file` already does (registry.py:265-271). Add a validator rule that flags `permissionMode: auto-edit` on an agent whose tools include neither Write nor Edit (currently true of `learning-analyst`).
test_strategy: Assert `validate_file` on an agent with `tools: [Read, NotARealTool]` produces an error naming `NotARealTool` (proving the list branch is checked), and on an agent with no `tools` key produces a warning. Add a roster-wide test that parses every file in `agents/` and asserts each declares a non-empty `tools` list and a `permissionMode`, with a narrow explicit allowlist for any agent intentionally granted the full surface — so a new agent cannot silently ship without a tool scope.

title: immune-untested-edges advertises test-stub generation it has no tools to perform
evidence:
`agents/immune-untested-edges.md:3-8` description: "...and generates minimal property-based test stubs for the worst offenders. Returns a JSON finding object with confidence and affected line numbers." Frontmatter at :11 grants `tools: Read, Grep, Glob` — no Write, no Edit. The body's "## Scanning procedure" (steps 1-4) only reads, estimates complexity, and prioritises; nothing generates stubs. Its output schema hard-codes `"auto_fix_directive": ""` (an empty string literal, unlike the sibling sweep agents which allow a populated directive), and `"untested-edges"` is absent from `AUTO_FIX_KINDS` in both `agent_baton/core/immune/sweeper.py:48-52` and `agent_baton/core/immune/triage.py:53-57`, so no downstream auto-fix agent produces the stubs either.

`agents/CLAUDE.md:19` states the `description` field "is what the orchestrator's router matches against — write it as a clear capability statement".
why_it_matters: The description is the routing surface. A task phrased "generate test stubs for untested branches" can route to this agent on the strength of a capability it structurally cannot deliver; it returns a JSON finding with an empty auto_fix_directive and the caller sees a no-op instead of an error. `agents/CLAUDE.md:24` also asks for one responsibility per agent — this description claims two, only one of which is implemented.
proposed_fix: Trim the description to what the agent does: detect high-complexity functions lacking test coverage and return a JSON finding. If stub generation is wanted, add `test-engineer` as the follow-up in the sweep pipeline rather than granting this haiku sweep agent Write access.
test_strategy: A roster consistency test asserting that any agent whose description contains generative verbs ("generates", "writes", "creates", "applies", "fixes") declares `Write` or `Edit` in its `tools` allowlist — this catches the class, not just this instance, and would also flag future read-only agents that over-promise.

title: SpecsPanel silently discards every spec the backend actually returns
why_it_matters: An operator with 40 approved specs in `~/.baton/central.db` opens the Specs tab and sees "0 specs", an empty table, and zero error text or console warning. They conclude their spec store is empty or their filters are wrong. Before 84ca0ab the panel crashed the whole app — visible and reported within a day. After it, the panel is permanently and quietly wrong, which is strictly harder to notice. It also violates the repo's own guiding principle #5 ("Could this functionality be failing silently?").
proposed_fix:
1. Fix the coercion to keep the array: `setSpecs(Array.isArray(res) ? res : res?.specs ?? [])`.
2. Correct `listSpecs`' declared return type to `Promise<Spec[]>` and delete `SpecListResponse` from `types.ts` (or narrow it to `Spec[] | {specs: Spec[]}` if the envelope is a real future shape).
3. Reconcile `Spec` (types.ts:448-460) with `SpecResponse` (specs.py:45-64): the backend emits `score_json: str`, not `score: SpecScore | null`, so `spec.score` at SpecsPanel.tsx:241 is always `undefined` — parse `score_json` in the client or change the backend to emit a structured `score`.
4. Replace the misleading comment with one that names `/api/v1/specs` and `routes/specs.py`.
test_strategy: Extend `SpecsPanel.test.tsx` with a test that mocks `api.listSpecs` with a NON-EMPTY bare array of two specs (the real backend shape) and asserts (a) `screen.findByText(/2 specs/)` and (b) both spec titles are in the document. That test must fail on the current `Array.isArray(res) ? []` line and pass after the fix. Add a matching backend contract test asserting `GET /api/v1/specs` returns a JSON array (not an object) so the two sides cannot drift again.

title: No React error boundary, and all six primary panels mount on every page load
evidence:
`grep -rn "ErrorBoundary|componentDidCatch|getDerivedStateFromError" pmo-ui/src pmo-ui/index.html` returns nothing. `main.tsx` mounts bare:

```tsx
createRoot(rootEl).render(<StrictMode><App /></StrictMode>);
```

And `App.tsx` does not conditionally render the main panels — it mounts them all and hides the inactive ones with CSS. The comment at App.tsx:218 says so explicitly: `{/* Main content — both views rendered simultaneously; CSS hides inactive one */}`. `KanbanBoard` (App.tsx:227), `ForgePanel` (App.tsx:243), `SpecsPanel` (App.tsx:257), `SpecQueuePanel` (App.tsx:267), `AgentWorkforceView` (App.tsx:275) and `BackOfHousePanel` (App.tsx:334) are all inside `style={{ display: view === 'x' ? 'block' : 'none' }}` wrappers — mounted and running their `useEffect` fetches regardless of the active tab.

That is precisely why a bug in a tab the user never opened blanked the entire app in 84ca0ab: `specs.find` threw during SpecsPanel's render, React unmounted the whole tree, and `#root` was left empty. Nothing about that blast radius changed — only the one `.find` call was patched. There is also no test that mounts `<App />` at all (the whole vitest suite is 3 files: `SpecsPanel`, `BeadGraphView`, `BeadTimelineView`).
why_it_matters: Any future throw during render in any of six panels — a `null` field in a board response, an unexpected enrichment shape from the spec queue, a bad date — takes down the entire PMO, including the Kanban board and Forge the user was actually working in. There is no partial degradation and no on-screen diagnostic; the operator gets a white page at `/pmo/` and must open devtools to learn anything.
proposed_fix: Add `pmo-ui/src/components/ErrorBoundary.tsx` (class component with `getDerivedStateFromError` + `componentDidCatch` logging to console) and wrap twice: once around `<App />` in `main.tsx` as the last-resort shell, and once per tabpanel `<div>` in `App.tsx` so a broken panel shows an inline "This panel failed to load — <error>" card while the rest of the PMO keeps working. Consider also gating the heavier panels behind `view === 'x' || visitedViews.has('x')` so an unopened tab cannot fetch or throw at all.
test_strategy: A vitest that renders `<App />` with `api.listSpecs` mocked to resolve a value that makes SpecsPanel throw during render, then asserts (a) the navbar brand text "Baton PMO" is still in the document (shell survived) and (b) an error-fallback string is present inside `#panel-specs`. It must fail today (the render throws out of `render()` and the tree is empty) and pass with the boundary in place.

title: Playwright e2e suite never navigates to the app — every goto('/') lands on the origin root, not /pmo/
why_it_matters: This is why the white-screen shipped. The repo carries thousands of lines of Playwright specs whose entire purpose is to catch a blank `/pmo/`, and not one of them ever requests `/pmo/`. The bug was found by a hand-rolled headless probe, per the commit message. Anyone running the suite gets either connection-refused noise or navigation to a non-existent route — never a real signal — so the suite provides negative value: it looks like coverage and is not.
proposed_fix:
1. `BasePage.goto`: `await this.page.goto(path || '.')` — or better, resolve explicitly: `await this.page.goto(new URL(path || '.', this.page.context()._options?.baseURL ?? '').href)`; simplest correct form is `page.goto(path)` with `path` defaulting to `''` (Playwright resolves `''` against the full baseURL).
2. Sweep `e2e/` replacing `goto('/')` with `goto()`.
3. Make `webServer.url` and the default `baseURL` agree (derive both from one constant), or drop `webServer` and require `PLAYWRIGHT_BASE_URL`.
4. Turn the connectivity test into a hard gate that asserts `#root` has non-trivial content and `page.on('pageerror')` recorded zero errors — the exact check the manual probe performed.
test_strategy: A unit-level assertion on the resolver (e.g. a small node test asserting `new URL(BasePage-resolved-path, baseURL).pathname === '/pmo/'`), plus a live smoke test that asserts `await page.locator('#root').innerHTML()` length is > 1000 and that no `pageerror` fired. Both must fail against a build with the SpecsPanel white-screen reintroduced.

title: Two of three spec lifecycle buttons call endpoints that do not exist; the third sends no body and 422s
evidence:
`SpecsPanel` exposes Review / Approve / Archive actions:

```ts
// SpecsPanel.tsx:220-229
if (action === 'approve')      { const res = await api.approveSpec(spec.spec_id); ... }
else if (action === 'review')  { const res = await api.markSpecReviewed(spec.spec_id); ... }
else                           { const res = await api.archiveSpec(spec.spec_id); ... }
```

The client targets `POST /api/v1/specs/{id}/review` (client.ts:331) and `POST /api/v1/specs/{id}/archive` (client.ts:347). `routes/specs.py` declares exactly four routes (lines 71, 89, 104, 114): list, create, get, approve. `grep -n "review|archive" agent_baton/api/routes/specs.py` returns nothing.

I mounted the router in a TestClient and probed it:
```
POST /api/v1/specs/x/review  -> 404
POST /api/v1/specs/x/archive -> 404
POST /api/v1/specs/x/approve (no body, Content-Type: application/json) -> 422
```
The 422 is because `approve_spec(spec_id: str, req: SpecApproveRequest)` (specs.py:114-115) requires a body, while `api.approveSpec` (client.ts:312-326) sends `method: 'POST'` with headers only and no `body`.

So all three lifecycle transitions the Specs panel offers are non-functional. The failures do surface (`setError` at SpecsPanel.tsx:231), but as raw `API 404:` / `API 422:` strings.
why_it_matters: A user clicks "Approve" on a reviewed spec and gets `API 422: {"detail":[{"type":"missing","loc":["body"]...}]}`. Clicking "Mark reviewed" or "Archive" gives `API 404: {"detail":"Not Found"}`. The Spec entity's entire state machine is unreachable from the UI — the panel is a read-only viewer wearing a workflow UI's clothes. Combined with finding #1 (the list is always empty), the Specs tab currently has no working capability at all.
proposed_fix:
Decide which side is authoritative and close the gap in one direction:
(a) Backend: add `POST /specs/{spec_id}/review` and `POST /specs/{spec_id}/archive` to `routes/specs.py` delegating to `store.update_state(spec_id, 'reviewed'|'archived', actor=...)`, mirroring `approve_spec`; and give `approve_spec`'s `req` a default (`req: SpecApproveRequest = SpecApproveRequest()`) so a bodyless POST is accepted. OR (b) Frontend: send `{actor}` bodies and hide Review/Archive behind a capability check until the routes land.
Either way, document the wire contract in `docs/api-reference.md` per pmo-ui/CLAUDE.md's "Backend coupling" rule, which was not followed here.
test_strategy: A pytest contract test over the real app asserting `POST /api/v1/specs/{id}/review`, `/archive` and `/approve` (with an empty JSON body) all return 2xx for a spec in a legal source state, plus a vitest that mocks a 404 from `markSpecReviewed` and asserts the panel renders a human-readable message rather than a raw `API 404:` string. The pytest must fail today (404/404/422).

title: The built PMO UI is never packaged, so `/pmo/` silently does not exist in an installed baton
evidence:
The mount is conditional and silent:

```python
# server.py:162-165
_pmo_dist = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent.parent / "pmo-ui" / "dist"
if _pmo_dist.is_dir():
    from fastapi.staticfiles import StaticFiles
    app.mount("/pmo", StaticFiles(directory=str(_pmo_dist), html=True), name="pmo-ui")
```

Nothing ever puts that directory there for an installed package. `pyproject.toml:87-89` is `[tool.setuptools.packages.find] include = ["agent_baton*"]` and `package-data` (lines 91-95) lists only `_bundled_agents/*.md` and `_bundled_visualize/*.html` — no pmo-ui. `MANIFEST.in` only *prunes* pmo-ui (`prune pmo-ui/src`, `prune pmo-ui/node_modules`) and never includes `pmo-ui/dist`. `pmo-ui/.gitignore` line 2 is `dist/`, and `git ls-files pmo-ui/dist` returns nothing, so the build output is neither committed nor generated by any install step (`scripts/build_dist.sh` has no pmo-ui reference — `grep -rn 'pmo-ui' pyproject.toml MANIFEST.in scripts/build_dist.sh` matched only the two MANIFEST prunes).

From site-packages the path resolves to `<site-packages>/pmo-ui/dist`, which cannot exist. Meanwhile `docs/api-reference.md:49` states: "PMO dashboard / React UI | API (the PMO UI ships as static files served at `/pmo/`)", and `pmo-ui/CLAUDE.md:3` says "Served at `/pmo/` by the FastAPI app."
why_it_matters: A user who `pip install`s agent-baton, runs `baton serve`, and opens `http://127.0.0.1:8741/pmo/` gets a 404 with no explanation. The server logs nothing — `is_dir()` is False and the branch is skipped without even a debug line. There is no documented `npm run build` prerequisite in the install path and no CLI diagnostic. The entire PMO UI domain is undeliverable to anyone who did not clone the repo and build by hand, which is exactly guiding principle #7 ("Does a user have the information needed to use this capability?") failing.
proposed_fix:
1. Emit a log line in the `else` branch: `_log.info("PMO UI not mounted — no built assets at %s. Run 'npm --prefix pmo-ui install && npm --prefix pmo-ui run build'.", _pmo_dist)`, and add a `/pmo/` fallback route returning that same message as HTML so the 404 is self-explaining.
2. Ship the built assets: move the build output under `agent_baton/_bundled_pmo_ui/` at build time, add it to `[tool.setuptools.package-data]`, and have `server.py` prefer the packaged path with the repo-relative path as a dev fallback. Add the `npm run build` step to `scripts/build_dist.sh`.
3. Add a `baton doctor` check for PMO UI asset presence.
test_strategy: A pytest that builds/inspects the wheel (or asserts `importlib.resources.files('agent_baton').joinpath('_bundled_pmo_ui/index.html').is_file()`) and a second test that creates the app with the assets directory absent and asserts `GET /pmo/` returns a 200/404 body containing the build instruction rather than a bare FastAPI `{"detail":"Not Found"}`. Both fail today.

title: checkEndpoint reports a missing endpoint as live, so Back-of-House shows LIVE badges for unconfigured integrations
evidence:
The helper contradicts its own contract:

```ts
/**
 * HEAD-ping an endpoint path (relative to /api/v1/pmo).
 * Resolves true if the server responds with a non-5xx status,
 * false if the endpoint is absent or the request fails.   <-- client.ts:473
 */
async checkEndpoint(path: string): Promise<boolean> {
  ...
  return res.status < 500;   // client.ts:484
}
```

`404 < 500` is `true`, so an absent endpoint reports live — the docstring's second clause is false for the exact case it names.

Worse, the probe targets are generic PMO routes, not integration health. `BohLoadingDock.tsx:33-70` sets `probeEndpoint: '/external-items?source=jira&status=open'` for Jira, `'...source=linear...'` for Linear, `'...source=github...'` for GitHub. `GET /pmo/external-items` exists unconditionally (`agent_baton/api/routes/pmo.py:2349`) and Starlette auto-serves HEAD for GET routes, so all three resolve `true` whether or not any Jira/Linear/GitHub credential is configured. The result is written straight into the badge at BohLoadingDock.tsx:390 (`{...i, liveStatus: result.live}`) and rendered as a LIVE/offline pill at BohLoadingDock.tsx:216.

The results are also persisted to `localStorage` under `pmo:boh-integrations` (BohLoadingDock.tsx:367-371), so a stale "live" state is shown on every subsequent load before the probe resolves.
why_it_matters: The Loading Dock is the operator's answer to "is my Jira wired up?". Today it answers "yes" for every integration on any running server, including ones with no credentials at all, because the probe measures whether baton's own generic route exists. An operator troubleshooting a missing Jira sync is actively misled away from the real cause.
proposed_fix:
1. Change the predicate to `res.ok` (or `res.status < 400`) and fix the docstring, so 404/405 correctly read as absent.
2. Replace the generic probes with per-integration liveness: either add `GET /api/v1/pmo/integrations` returning configured-adapter status from the backend adapter registry, or probe a source-specific route and require a non-empty/`configured: true` payload rather than mere reachability.
3. Do not persist `liveStatus` to localStorage — it is ephemeral runtime state; keep only user-controlled `connected` in the persisted slice.
test_strategy: A vitest that mocks `fetch` to resolve `{status: 404}` and asserts `api.checkEndpoint('/anything')` is `false` (fails today, returns `true`), plus a component test mounting `BohLoadingDock` with a 404-returning probe and asserting the Jira row renders the offline badge, not LIVE.

title: pmo-ui/CLAUDE.md documents a non-existent npm script and a non-existent type generator
evidence:
`pmo-ui/CLAUDE.md:38` instructs `npm run e2e          # Playwright (requires the FastAPI app running)`. `grep -n '"e2e"' pmo-ui/package.json` returns nothing — the scripts block (package.json:7-16) defines `test:e2e`, `test:e2e:ui`, `test:e2e:smoke`, `test:e2e:report`, but no bare `e2e`. Any agent or human following the file verbatim gets `npm ERR! Missing script: "e2e"`.

`pmo-ui/CLAUDE.md:24` states: "Generated API types live in `src/api/types.ts`. Don't hand-edit shapes that mirror backend models — regenerate or edit the matching `agent_baton/api/models/*.py` and re-derive." There is no generator anywhere: `ls scripts/` shows only `build_dist.sh`, `install.sh/ps1`, `sync_bundled_agents.sh` and three python one-shots; no openapi-typescript dependency exists in `package.json`; and `types.ts` demonstrably contains hand-written shapes with no backend counterpart (`SpecListResponse` at types.ts:462 mirrors nothing in `agent_baton/api/models/responses.py`).
why_it_matters: This is the file every Claude Code agent dispatched into `pmo-ui/` reads first. It tells them to run a command that errors, and to "re-derive" types via a pipeline that does not exist — so agents either invent a generator, silently hand-edit anyway (which is how the fictional `SpecListResponse` in finding #1 survived), or waste turns hunting for tooling. The instruction that would have prevented finding #1 is unactionable as written.
proposed_fix: Fix line 38 to `npm run test:e2e` (and note the `PLAYWRIGHT_BASE_URL` requirement). Rewrite line 24 to state the truth: types.ts is hand-maintained and MUST be verified against the FastAPI route's declared `response_model` — with an explicit checklist entry "confirm the route returns an envelope vs a bare list". Optionally make the claim true by adding an `openapi-typescript` script wired to `/openapi.json` and a CI drift check.
test_strategy: A CI/lint step that extracts fenced `npm run <script>` invocations from `pmo-ui/CLAUDE.md` and asserts each name exists in `package.json.scripts` — it fails today on `e2e`. For the types claim, a schema-drift test that fetches the app's `/openapi.json` and asserts every `Spec*` interface in `types.ts` has a matching component schema.

title: CI runs only 3.4% of the test suite while docs claim the full suite is CI-gated
evidence:
`.github/workflows/tests.yml` has exactly two pytest steps. Line 52 is collection-only: `run: python -m pytest --co -q`. The only executing step (lines 54-72) enumerates a fixed allowlist:

```yaml
      - name: Bead suite (exercises the bd backend end-to-end)
        env:
          BATON_BD_BACKEND: bd
        run: |
          python -m pytest -p no:cacheprovider -q \
            tests/test_bead_cli.py \
            ... \
            tests/storage/ \
            tests/static/test_no_direct_bead_store_construction.py
```

Measured: `python -m pytest --co -q` on that exact allowlist collects **336 tests**; `python -m pytest --co -q` on the repo collects **9828 tests** — 3.4%. Nothing under `tests/engine/` (state machine, executor, dispatcher), `tests/govern/` (compliance chain, evidence bundles, policy, redaction), `tests/planning/`, `tests/orchestration/`, `tests/api/`, `tests/cli/`, `tests/integration/`, or `tests/e2e/` is executed. The workflow's own header comment concedes this ("widen the test selection over time as the broader suite is hardened for CI") but both CLAUDE.md files state the opposite: `tests/CLAUDE.md:48` — "The full suite is gated to maintainers + CI." and `CLAUDE.md:110` — "The full suite is gated to maintainers + CI."
why_it_matters: Root CLAUDE.md forbids agents from running the full suite (`CLAUDE.md:110`) on the stated grounds that CI covers it. Since CI does not, no automated actor ever exercises the governance and engine paths. This is not hypothetical: commit 68ffc12 (`Couple roster to phase policy on the complexity-override path`) changed `stages/decomposition.py` and left 4 tests in `tests/planning/test_plan_quality_golden.py` failing on HEAD — it passed CI because `tests/planning/` is not in the allowlist. Any future change to `evidence_bundle.py`, `compliance.py`, or `executor.py` can break tamper-evidence or the state machine and merge green.
proposed_fix: Add a second CI job that runs the whole suite (`python -m pytest -q`) on PRs, keeping the existing bd job as a fast pre-check. If some directories are genuinely not CI-hardened, deselect them explicitly with `--ignore=` and register a pytest marker so the exclusion list is visible and shrinkable — then correct `tests/CLAUDE.md:48` and `CLAUDE.md:110` to state exactly which directories CI covers rather than claiming full coverage.
test_strategy: A meta-test (e.g. `tests/static/test_ci_covers_suite.py`) that parses `.github/workflows/tests.yml`, extracts every path/`--ignore` argument passed to pytest, and asserts that the set of top-level directories under `tests/` not covered by any CI job is empty (or exactly equals a small, explicitly-listed allowlist constant). The test must fail if a new `tests/<dir>/` is added without CI coverage.

title: Golden planner snapshot suite is red on HEAD; one case raises PlanQualityError through the public planner API
evidence:
`python -m pytest tests/planning/test_plan_quality_golden.py -q` on branch HEAD (09f8098) gives `4 failed, 2 passed`: `compound-multi-concern`, `high-risk-security`, `compliance-audit`, `knowledge-heavy`. Three are snapshot mismatches at `tests/planning/test_plan_quality_golden.py:123` (`assert _normalize_plan(plan) == _load_snapshot(case_id)`). The fourth is not a stale snapshot — it is an unhandled exception from production code, reproducible outside pytest:

```
$ python -c "from agent_baton.core.engine.planner import IntelligentPlanner; IntelligentPlanner().create_plan('Use project security knowledge to update JWT authentication guidance and tests', explicit_knowledge_packs=['security-pack'])"
PlanQualityError: Plan ...-jwt-authe-0a3a4278 blocked by ValidationStage: [critical] agent_phase_mismatch: phase_id=2 phase='Implement' step_id=2.1 agent='security-reviewer'. Reviewer-class agents are blocked from implementation phases.
```

Git history shows the cause: `2720191` (RiskStage phase-slot guarantee) regenerated `tests/snapshots/plans/compliance-audit.json`, then `68ffc12` changed `stages/decomposition.py` (reviewer filtering on the complexity-override path) and touched no snapshot and no golden test — its commit message only cites `tests/e2e/test_manager_mode_planning.py`.
why_it_matters: `baton plan` is the documented entry point for every orchestrated task (`CLAUDE.md` "Orchestrator behavior (mandatory)" step 1). For a security/knowledge-flavoured prompt the planner now emits a plan that its own ValidationStage rejects as critical, so the command aborts with a traceback instead of producing `plan.json`. Additionally, a red golden suite trains maintainers to ignore it, so it stops functioning as a regression net for plan shape at all.
proposed_fix: Fix the product defect first: on the complexity-override path in `stages/decomposition.py`, the reviewer-class filter must be applied consistently with the phase list actually produced, so a `security-reviewer` never lands in an Implement phase (or a Review phase is guaranteed when a reviewer stays on the roster). Only then regenerate the three snapshots under `tests/snapshots/plans/`, and add a `make regen-golden` target plus a note in `tests/CLAUDE.md` so the regeneration step is discoverable.
test_strategy: Two assertions. (1) A behavioural test independent of snapshots: for each of the 6 GOLDEN_CASES prompts, `IntelligentPlanner().create_plan(...)` must not raise, and for every phase whose name matches an implementation phase, no step's agent may be in `REVIEWER_AGENTS`. (2) The existing snapshot parametrisation must pass 6/6 after regeneration. Test (1) must fail on the current `decomposition.py` and pass after the fix.

title: Deferred-feature acceptance tests assert on source-file substrings and probe file paths that do not exist
evidence:
All three tests in this file are `@pytest.mark.xfail(..., strict=False)` and none of them execute the code they claim to verify — they `read_text()` a source file and assert a substring is present. `test_executor_blocks_advancement_on_veto` (line 29) ends with `assert found, "executor does not yet read blocks_execution / parsed_verdict"` after grepping module sources for `"blocks_execution" in src or "parsed_verdict" in src`. It now XPASSes: `pytest tests/govern/test_phase0_deferred.py -q -rX` → `2 xfailed, 1 xpassed`, with `XPASS ... test_executor_blocks_advancement_on_veto`. Because `strict=False`, XPASS is not a failure and nothing tells anyone bd-f606 is done.

Worse, `test_knowledge_resolver_emits_telemetry` (line 115) probes:
```python
    candidates = [
        repo_root / "agent_baton" / "core" / "knowledge" / "resolver.py",
        repo_root / "agent_baton" / "core" / "knowledge" / "knowledge_resolver.py",
        repo_root / "agent_baton" / "core" / "learn" / "retrospective.py",

```
None of these three paths exist in the repo. The real modules are `agent_baton/core/engine/knowledge_resolver.py` (line 296: `self._telemetry.record_used(`) and `agent_baton/core/observe/retrospective.py` (line 261: `self._telemetry.record_outcome(`) — i.e. bd-32d3 landed, but the test can never pass.
why_it_matters: The file's docstring promises "once the follow-up beads land they should flip to PASS without test changes" — that promise is false in both directions. bd-f606's grep passes on mere textual presence of `blocks_execution` while proving nothing about VETO enforcement, and bd-32d3's test is permanently red on dead paths, so the bead looks perpetually open. Anyone auditing governance readiness from this file gets the wrong answer for two of three items. A real behavioural VETO test does exist (`tests/test_executor_veto_enforcement.py`), so this file is now pure misleading scaffolding.
proposed_fix: Delete `tests/govern/test_phase0_deferred.py`. bd-f606 is covered behaviourally by `tests/test_executor_veto_enforcement.py`; add equivalent behavioural tests for bd-c44c (assert a `UsageLogger.log()` call produces a `usage_records` row with non-null `team_id`/`org_id`/`cost_center`) and bd-32d3 (assert `KnowledgeResolver.resolve()` with an injected `KnowledgeTelemetryStore` writes a `knowledge_telemetry` row). Each must fail if the corresponding production wiring is removed — which the current grep tests do not (renaming a comment would satisfy them).

title: Two env-var tables both claim to be the full mirrored list, disagree with each other, and omit ~19 live variables
evidence:
`docs/cli-reference.md:2943` — "The full list of Baton environment variables. The same table is mirrored in [references/baton-engine.md](../references/baton-engine.md#environment-variables)." `references/baton-engine.md:2336` makes the reciprocal claim. Parsing both tables:
- present only in `docs/cli-reference.md`: `BATON_BD_BACKEND`, `BATON_BD_BIN`, `BATON_BD_ENABLED`, `BATON_BD_PREFIX`, `BATON_WORKTREE_STALE_HOURS`
- present only in `references/baton-engine.md`: `BATON_COMPLIANCE_FAIL_CLOSED`, `BATON_PLAN_REVIEW`, `BATON_POLICY_FAIL_CLOSED`, `BATON_SKIP_GIT_NOTES_SETUP`
(15 vs 14 rows). Against the code, `grep -rhoE 'BATON_[A-Z0-9_]+' agent_baton/` yields 33 names absent from the root `CLAUDE.md` table, and these are entirely undocumented in any public doc, `README.md`, or `templates/`: `BATON_REDACTION_ENABLED`, `BATON_DEFAULT_STEP_TIMEOUT_S`, `BATON_OVERRIDE_PROMPT`, `BATON_CONFLICT_PREDICT`, `BATON_WORKTREE_ROOT`.

`BATON_REDACTION_ENABLED` is a governance kill-switch: `agent_baton/core/govern/_redaction.py:266` — `raw = os.environ.get("BATON_REDACTION_ENABLED", "1")` — and the module docstring (line 12) states redaction is applied inside `ComplianceChainWriter.append` "so that hashed entries are *already* redacted on disk". Setting it to `0` writes unredacted PII/secrets into the hash-chained audit log, and no user-facing doc mentions it.

Separately, `references/baton-engine.md:2350` documents `BATON_SKIP_GIT_NOTES_SETUP` as silencing "the runtime warning emitted by `NotesAdapter.write()`". `NotesAdapter` no longer exists — `agent_baton/core/exec/runner.py:6` says "ADR-13b WP-G: git-notes (NotesAdapter) was removed" and `grep -rn NotesAdapter agent_baton/ --include=*.py` returns only comments. The variable is now read solely by `scripts/install.sh:335`.
why_it_matters: `references/baton-engine.md` is a distributable reference copied to `~/.claude/references/` by `install.sh` and read by orchestrator agents as the engine protocol contract (per root CLAUDE.md). An agent consulting it for the compliance fail-closed switch finds `BATON_COMPLIANCE_FAIL_CLOSED`; one consulting `docs/cli-reference.md` — the doc that calls itself the full list — does not, and would ship a regulated-domain run silently fail-open. Meanwhile the redaction kill-switch that can leak secrets into the audit chain is invisible to operators.
proposed_fix: Make one table canonical (`docs/cli-reference.md`) and replace the other with a link rather than a copy. Backfill every `BATON_*` name actually read by `agent_baton/` — starting with `BATON_REDACTION_ENABLED`, `BATON_DEFAULT_STEP_TIMEOUT_S`, `BATON_OVERRIDE_PROMPT`, `BATON_CONFLICT_PREDICT`, `BATON_WORKTREE_ROOT`. Delete the `NotesAdapter.write()` clause from `references/baton-engine.md:2350` and scope the row to `scripts/install.sh`.
test_strategy: A doc-sync test that (a) regex-extracts every `os.environ.get("BATON_...")` / `os.environ["BATON_..."]` literal from `agent_baton/**/*.py` and asserts each appears as a row in `docs/cli-reference.md`'s Environment Variables table, and (b) asserts `references/baton-engine.md` contains no duplicate env table (only a link). It must fail today on `BATON_REDACTION_ENABLED` and pass after backfill.

title: docs/cli-reference.md claims to document every command but omits 12 shipped commands entirely
evidence:
`docs/cli-reference.md:3` — "Complete command reference for the `baton` CLI. Every command, flag, and option is documented here with syntax, defaults, and usage examples." `docs/CLAUDE.md` reinforces it: `cli-reference.md` | "Reference for every `baton <command>`", and the change matrix says "New CLI command or flag → `cli-reference.md`".

`baton --help` advertises 90 subcommands. `grep -c "baton <cmd>" docs/cli-reference.md` returns **0** for: `run`, `finops`, `tenancy`, `merge`, `users`, `release`, `viz`, `webhook`, `slo`, `souls`, `handoff`, `quickstart`. All are real and registered — e.g. `baton quickstart --help` → `[--name NAME] [--dry-run]`, `baton run --help` → `[--plan PLAN] [--task-id TASK_ID] [--max-parallel N] [--dry-run] [--resume]`, `baton slo --help` → `{define,list,measure,burns,seed-defaults}`.

Searching all of `docs/` and `README.md`, five of these — `merge`, `users`, `viz`, `slo`, `quickstart` — appear in **no** public doc at all; `run` appears only inside `docs/specs/agent-baton-claude-code-middle-manager-prd-tdd.md`. Because the page asserts completeness, a reader who cannot find `baton run` reasonably concludes it does not exist.

It must fail today naming `run`, `quickstart`, `merge`, `users`, `viz`, `slo`, and pass once documented.

title: The only test validating the 30 distributable agent definitions silently skips based on the working directory
evidence:
`tests/test_validator.py:278-289`:
```python
    @pytest.mark.parametrize("agents_dir_str", ["agents", ".claude/agents"])
    def test_agents_in_directory_pass(self, validator, agents_dir_str):
        agents_dir = Path(agents_dir_str)
        if not agents_dir.is_dir():
            pytest.skip(f"{agents_dir_str}/ directory not found (not running from repo root)")
        results = validator.validate_directory(agents_dir)
        assert len(results) > 0
        for r in results:
            assert r.valid, f"{r.path}: {r.errors}"
```
`Path("agents")` is relative to the process CWD, not the test file. Demonstrated:
```
$ cd /home/user/agent-baton/agent_baton && python -m pytest ../tests/test_validator.py -q -rs
SKIPPED [1] ../tests/test_validator.py:285: agents/ directory not found (not running from repo root)
SKIPPED [1] ../tests/test_validator.py:285: .claude/agents/ directory not found (not running from repo root)
30 passed, 2 skipped
```
The suite reports green with zero agent files validated. The `.claude/agents` parameterisation additionally always skips in CI, since root `CLAUDE.md` records `.claude/` as "Project-specific orchestration setup (not committed)". The same CWD-relative pattern appears at `tests/orchestration/test_stack_detection.py:130` (`pytest.skip("repo root does not contain pyproject.toml — wrong layout")`).
why_it_matters: `agents/` holds the 30 distributable agent definitions that `install.sh` copies into user projects; this is the only test asserting they all parse and validate. It disappears without any failure signal whenever pytest is invoked from a subdirectory (a normal habit when working inside `agent_baton/`, and the pattern the repo's own token-efficiency rules encourage). A malformed frontmatter field could ship to users with the suite green. Neighbouring tests in the same file already do it correctly — e.g. `tests/test_router.py:369-371` resolves `Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent`.
proposed_fix: Anchor to the repo root: `ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]` and use `ROOT / agents_dir_str`. Keep the skip only for `.claude/agents` (legitimately absent), and make the `agents` case unconditional — a missing `agents/` directory should fail, not skip. Apply the same anchoring at `tests/orchestration/test_stack_detection.py:130`. Consider a session-scoped `repo_root` fixture in `tests/conftest.py` so this pattern is available everywhere.
test_strategy: Run `pytest tests/test_validator.py -rs` from a subdirectory (e.g. `agent_baton/`) and assert zero skips and that `test_agents_in_directory_pass[agents]` passes. A stronger guard: assert `len(results) == 30` so the test also fails if the directory resolves to something empty rather than merely non-existent.
